title: BisaApi
description: Generated by `just gen-types` — do not edit by hand.

statement.description:
The outcome, in the author's words. Sharpened before a run starts but
never rewritten silently — each change carries a `kind:3400` note.

workflow.description:
The workflow the next run will use — or the one the current run is a
copy of. `None` until one is picked, proposed or adopted.

run.description:
The current run: the live one, else the latest that started. A goal
may run several times over its life, one live at a time; a run made
while one is live is queued and never the current run until it starts.

runs.description:
The queued runs and the newest [`GOAL_RUNS_KEPT`], oldest first — the
queued ones at the tail. The index holds every run the goal has had.

listening.description:
The goal's standing while its workflow begins on events: the inputs
its event runs bind, since when, and — after a failed run or a spent
budget — why it paused. `None` for a goal whose work begins by hand.

closed.description: Set once, by closing. The first of the two moves a goal makes on its own.

archived.description:
Put away: hidden from every list that does not ask, and only ever
after closing — the second move, and the one that goes back.

origin.description: How this goal came to exist. Recorded at capture, never edited.

mode.description:
How the goal moves: who designs its workflow, and who adopts, starts
and repairs it. See [`GoalMode`].

assignees.description:
Who carries this goal: agents take the work, humans may decide the
gates, teams expand to both. Descendants inherit through `origin`.
The agents and teams named here are also the staff the Workflow
Agent designs from — a team whole or one of its members — and when
none is named, the nearest ancestor's, else every enabled one.

revision.description:
Monotonic snapshot revision. Only a snapshot with a higher revision may
replace state.

created_at.description: Unix seconds of creation (assigned at the store edge).

Goal.description:
A signed, durable record of a wanted outcome. The current snapshot of the
addressable `kind:33400` event; history lives in the journal, and
`revision` is the snapshot authority (monotonic, never reused).

`deny_unknown_fields`: a goal written by the lifecycle-shaped code carried
`state`, `criteria`, `contract`, `blocked` and `parent`, and this build
refuses it rather than half-reading it.

PrincipalId.description: secp256k1 public key, 64 lowercase hex chars

inputs.description:
The values the host gave when it began listening: what every run its
events start binds, beneath what a start's mapping reads off the event.

budget.description:
Each run's own ceiling — a library workflow's; a goal's runs spend
against the goal's budget. Absent, the workspace default applies.

Listening.description:
A host's standing: listening since when, with which inputs for the runs
its events start, under which per-run budget — and why it paused, when a
failed run or a spent budget paused it. Kept apart from a workflow's
definition, so turning a workflow On or Off is never a revision of it.

Budget.description: Hard ceilings. `None` = unlimited (still tracked in the ledger).

Paused.description: Why a host stopped hearing its events without being turned off.

oneOf.description:
A run the events started failed: nothing more starts until a repair is
adopted or the person says *listen again*.
The goal's budget is spent.
Given up on. No further work will be done.
Replaced by another goal, which is named.

Closure.description: Why and when a goal was closed.

Archived.description: When a record was archived — unix seconds.

oneOf.description: A person captured it.

A `spawn` step of a goal's run, or an agent's `spawn_sub_goal`,
refining a parent.

A `spawn` step of a run of the workspace: a goal of its own, refining
nothing, that the step may wait on. History like every origin — the
run may since be gone with its workflow.

GoalOrigin.description: How a goal came to exist.

StepId.description: A step id: 1-32 chars of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', starting with a letter

GoalMode.description:
How a goal moves — chosen at capture, from `goals.default_mode`.

- `Auto`: the Workflow Agent designs the workflow, and the platform adopts
  it, starts the run, repairs a failed run and restarts by itself; the
  run is unattended, so a tool permission above the step's tier ceiling
  that no guard rule decides is read by the classifier
  (`goals.auto.permissions`) rather than put to a person, and every
  step's agent is told to decide rather than ask. Only what a person
  alone can do waits for one: a `human`, `approval` or `wait { release }`
  step the workflow declares, the guard's `ask` and `deny`, a call the
  classifier finds harmful or gives no verdict on, a push or a pull
  request under a gated project, a question an agent still chooses to
  ask, a design whose required inputs have no default, and a goal
  repaired more times than `goals.auto.repair_limit` allows.
- `Guided`: the Workflow Agent proposes; the person adopts, asks for
  changes or declines, and approves every amendment.
- `Manual`: the person designs on the goal's Workflow tab, with the
  Workflow Agent on request — a proposal it makes is the goal's own
  draft, never a gate.

oneOf.description: An `AgentDef` id. Takes work.

A human principal. Decides gates and answers questions; a human-only
assignment never blocks execution.

A `TeamDef` id, expanded to its members at resolution time. Nesting is
not modelled: one level needs no cycle detection.

Assignee.description:
A principal-shaped target for work or approval.

Serialization matches the store's `TeamMember` exactly (`{"agent": "id"}`,
`{"human": "<hex>"}`), so a team's member list and an assignee list are the
same bytes on the wire.

Tags.description: Normalized categories: lowercase a-z, 0-9 and '-', sorted and deduplicated

sha256.description: Lowercase hex. The blob's address, and the proof of what it contains.

name.description:
What the sender called it. Display only — it is **never** a path, and
nothing joins it to a directory.

mime.description:
The media type the sender declared. Display and harness routing only:
the byte route re-checks the actual bytes before serving anything
inline, because a claim about a file is not evidence about it.

AttachmentRef.description:
One file carried by a message.

Rides an `imeta` tag on the message event, follows NIP-92/94's shape, and is
the same struct the HTTP body, the index row and the harness input use —
there is deliberately not a second spelling of it per layer.

GoalDocumentRow.description:
One of a goal's documents as the goal page lists it: the descriptor as
given, the name it is kept under, its absolute path, and whether the
bytes — and so the file — are on this node.

Fate.description: What becomes of a thing: left as it is, put away, or gone.

GoalPlan.description:
The choice for a goal: its own fate (archive or delete — never keep), the
fate of the projects born of it, and whether a deleted project's managed
folder goes to the Trash.

WorkflowPlan.description: The choice for a workflow, the same shape.

adopted.description: An adopted folder: its records may go, its folder never moves.

workstream_ids.description:
Its workstreams by id — the desktop counts the terminals it has
rooted there, which the node never knows.

ProjectFacts.description: A project as the preview lists it: enough to weigh its fate.

unsettled_sessions.description:
Rows still live when the wait ran out: their process was told and
their row is aborted; the retirement did not wait longer.

workstreams_retired.description: The workstreams whose records went or were put away — the desktop closes the shells rooted at them.

name.description: The cache's stable name, e.g. `harness.listing`.

hit_rate.description: Hits ÷ (hits + misses), 0 when never read — the panel's headline number.

live_steps.description: Steps running or waiting right now — cancelled with the run.

RunFacts.description:
A run that is going — a goal's, or a workflow's in the workspace — as the
preview names it.

oneOf.description:
Made behind its goal's live run; starts on its own, in order, when the
goal has none. A run of the workspace is never queued.

RunStatus.description: A projection of the records, never stored as truth.

id.description: The holder's own id — where a client navigates to detach.

label.description:
What a person reads: the team's name, the goal's title, the
workflow's name. A row that renders as a bare ULID tells the reader
nothing.

live.description:
In motion: a goal whose unfinished run is of this workflow. The
designer is read-only while any holder is live.

Reference.description:
One place an object is referenced. A row of `GET /usage/{kind}/{id}`, and
one of the things the matching `DELETE` refuses over.

oneOf.description:
A workflow's step names this object — a start event's, too — or a
goal runs it.
A `Listed` gate policy names this object; the `id` is the gate.
A connector account on this machine still uses the connector.

ReferenceKind.description:
What kind of thing holds a reference, as `GET /usage/{kind}/{id}` reports
it. Mirrors the store's `ReferenceKind` one variant at a time so the wire
contract is a decision here rather than a leak of an internal enum.

ArchiveBody.description: `POST /goals/{id}/archive`, `/workflows/{wfid}/archive`, `/projects/{pid}/archive`: put away, or taken back out.

InitRepositoryBody.description:
`POST /projects/{pid}/git/init`: the same `[key, value]` local git config a
creation request can name, applied to the new repository; empty for none.

InitRepositoryReply.description:
What `POST /projects/{pid}/git/init` answers: the project as it now reads
(a row) and the committer policy's one sentence, when it had something to
say — `null` when the repository already had an identity of its own.

path.description:
Where the files are — resolved, so an `External` root shows its real
path rather than a managed one that does not exist.

workstreams.description: Workstreams recorded against this project, in any state.

goals.description: Every goal this project is attached to.

ProjectRow.description:
A row of `GET /goals/{id}/projects` — and of `GET /projects`, which
answers the workspace-wide question with the same shape.

A project belongs to the workspace, not to a goal; `goals` is
the whole of its relationship to any of them — the attachments — and a
project with none is a standalone project, which is an ordinary thing to
be.

id.description: Stable across renames — the slug may change, this may not.

slug.description: The directory name under `projects/`. Unique workspace-wide.

origin.description:
Where it was born — the workspace, a goal, or a workflow's step.
History, never ownership: attachment stays the one relation, and this
survives the deletion of whatever it names.

group.description:
A person's grouping of projects in the rail — one level, free text.
Display only: nothing resolves through it and the index does not hold it.

photo.description:
A picture for the project: an attachment by content hash, served by
`GET /attachments/{sha256}?as=image`. Display only.

archived.description:
Put away: out of the rail and the pickers, refused for an attachment
or an agent step's placement; the folder and every record stay.

Slug.description: A directory name: 1-64 chars of lowercase a-z, 0-9, '-' or '_', starting with a letter or digit

oneOf.description: `projects/<slug>/tree` — created and owned by Bisa.

An existing folder anywhere on disk, adopted by reference. The platform
never writes its own scratch into it.
A plain folder. Work in it isolates by copy, not by worktree.

host.description: The instance — `github.com`, or a host of the person's own.

owner_repo.description: `owner/repo` — the whole namespace, then the name.

CodeHost.description:
The code host behind a repository's `origin`, recorded when the project is
made: which kind (`github` · `gitlab` · `bitbucket` — the code host crate's
words), which instance, and the repository's path on it. A record, not a
live fact: the Connection card reads the remote again.

oneOf.description: A person made it with no goal in hand.

Made from a goal — by a person on the goal's surfaces or `--goal`, by
an agent in a goal's session outside any step, or by a step of the
goal's own design (`step` names it then).

Made by an agent running one step of a library workflow — on a goal
(`goal` names it), or in a run of the workspace (no goal at all).

ProjectOrigin.description:
Where a project came from. **Never an owner**: the goal ⇄ project
attachment stays the one relation, and
this is history — recorded once at creation, surviving the deletion of
whatever it names, resolved through by nothing.

A project made by a step sits with what the step's workflow belongs to
: a step of the **goal's own design** makes the goal's project
(`Goal`, with the step named); a step of a **library** workflow — reused
across goals, run in the workspace, or begun by one of its start events —
makes the workflow's (`Step`).

Read by hand: `Step` flattens its [`StepRef`], and a derived `flatten` of
a struct lets a key nobody knows drop in silence, whatever the struct's
own rule says — so the keys are held to the variant's list first
([`crate::workflow::refuse_unknown_keys`]), then read.

StepRef.description:
The step that made a project: which run, which step, of which workflow.
Kept whichever tab the project sits in, because *who made this*
is history worth keeping even when the project is filed under its goal.

oneOf.description: No agent may publish; a person may.
Allowed, through the `Publish` gate.
Allowed without a gate. The default.

PublishPolicy.description:
How a branch leaves this machine. Pushing, opening and merging a pull
request are outward actions. The default is `Auto` — a new project publishes
without a gate (the owner's chosen default); a person can require a
gate, or forbid publishing, per project in the repository panel.

GoalDocumentsBody.description: `POST /goals/{id}/documents`: more documents for a goal that exists.

oneOf.description: No run, or the last run was cancelled: a workflow can start.

Every live step is waiting — on a person, a signal or the clock — or
the goal is listening for the event that starts its next run.

GoalStatus.description:
Where a goal stands. A projection of its run and its closure — six words
for rows and screens, none of them a state anything writes.

oneOf.description:
A question, an approval, a release, an adoption — or a workflow chosen
and not started. Your move.
An agent or a check is working.
A signal, a schedule, a delay, or a child goal: the outside world.
The run finished, or the goal is closed.
No workflow yet: the goal is still being designed.

Holder.description:
Who a goal waits on right now — the one word the Goals screen, the CLI
and the inbox all print. A projection like [`GoalStatus`], never stored:
the caller gathers the run and whether anything durable names the goal
(`owed` — a pending gate, a question), and this decides.

oneOf.description: Drawn for the library by a person in this workspace.
Installed from the bundled catalog, under this slug.
Designed for one goal, and shown there rather than in the library.

WorkflowOrigin.description:
Where a workflow came from.

A separate type from [`Origin`] because a workflow has a case the others
cannot hold: a design drawn for **one goal** — the Workflow Agent's
proposal, or the goal's own Workflow tab. A goal-scoped design is the
goal's, not the library's: the Workflows destination and every picker show
the library (`Workspace` and `Catalog`) and leave a goal's designs on the
goal, and promoting one to the library is an explicit copy.

GoalEdge.description:
Typed edge in the goal graph. One kind: `refines`. The three that had no
writer (`depends_on`, `informs`, `supersedes`) are gone; `Superseded { by }`
on the closure reason carries the last one's relation.

oneOf.description: `from` is a sub-goal decomposing `to`.

steps.description: Display order. The graph is in each step's `then`.

origin.description:
Drawn for the library, installed from the catalog, or designed for
one goal — where the library, the pickers and the goal's own tab each
show it follows from this.

archived.description:
Put away: out of the library and the pickers, refused for a goal or a
run; the runs that hold a copy are untouched.

decision_making.description:
Whether the Decision-Making Agent stands in at the decision points a
run of this workflow reaches — who takes a step's work item, whether an
auto goal adopts it alone — when the workspace has not switched it on
for all. A `judge` step asks it either way.

revision.description:
Monotonic; every save is a revision. A run holds the copy it started
with, so a later revision never touches it.

Workflow.description:
A workflow: inputs, steps, and the flows between them. The addressable
`kind:33412` snapshot; `revision` is the snapshot authority.

oneOf.description: `agent:<id>`, `team:<id>` or `human:<hex>`, in wire form.
A project id.

An account of one connector, by id — this machine's way into an
outside platform, which a template cannot know. The connector is
absent while the designer has not chosen one: a problem
(`ProblemKind::Unfilled`), never a refusal.

InputDef.description:
A typed input a run is started with. A template cannot know a project's
ULID or a workspace's people, so a placement or an assignee that varies
per goal is an input, and a step names the input ([`ValueRef::Input`]).

Deserialization refuses a key it does not know — a misspelled `defualt`
is an error the author sees, not a default that silently never applies.
The kind sits flattened beside the other fields, which is why the check
is written by hand ([`refuse_unknown_keys`]) rather than derived.

InputName.description: A input name: 1-32 chars of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', starting with a letter

ConnectorId.description: A connector id: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', '.', ':'

then.description:
What follows. Several flows fan out in parallel; a flow labelled with
a branch is taken only when a gateway chose that branch, or when a
boundary event of that name diverted the step.

boundaries.description:
Events heard while this step is live — a timeout that diverts it, a
reminder posted beside it, a message or a signal that ends it — on the
kinds whose work can be stopped ([`may_carry_boundaries`]). A divert's
flows are the ones labelled with its name.

join.description:
How several incoming flows meet. Irrelevant with one. A loop edge —
a flow back into this step from a step it leads to — never holds an
`all` or a `one` join: the step enters on its forward flows, and the
loop edge re-enters it when taken.

on_fail.description: What a failure of this step does once its retries are spent.

retries.description: How many times a failed attempt is retried before `on_fail` applies.

max_visits.description:
How many times this step may be entered in one run. A loop is legal;
an unbounded one is not.

position.description:
Where the card stands on the designer's canvas, in canvas pixels.
Absent, the layered layout places it — the same way on every machine
— until a person moves it or edits the canvas, which writes every
card's place. The run machine and validation never read it.

oneOf.description:
One way a run begins: by hand, or on an event ([`StartOn`]). Done the
moment the run enters it. Several are several ways in: a run enters
the one it began at and the others are skipped. `inputs` maps the
event onto the run's inputs — templates reading `{event.<path>}` and
nothing else, the one place the event is read — and `guard` says what
an occurrence does while runs it started are still live. A `manual`
start maps nothing and has no guard.

A work item run by an agent: the existing executor, placement and
harness walk. Completes when the item yields a result.

model.description:
A model pin for this step's sessions. **Never substituted**: an
unavailable pin fails the step rather than running something the
author did not ask for. Absent means the agent's own plan.

effort.description:
An effort pin for this step's sessions: a level, or `auto` for
the Decision-Making Agent to name one. It wins over the model's
own and the agent's plan, and is then clamped to what the harness
and the model take. Absent means the agent's own.

oneOf.description:
A person answers — from the options offered, in free text, or "not
sure" — or does something by hand and marks the step done.

A signed decision under the workspace's `approval` policy. Declined is
a failure of the step.

Pass or fail, judged by a command or by a schema over an upstream
output. A check that does not pass is a failure of the step.

`pick = "first"` (the default): the first rule whose condition holds
names the branch. `pick = "every"`: every rule that holds does, and
their flows are all taken at once. `otherwise` when none holds. Only
the chosen branches' flows are taken.
`yes` when `when` holds, else `no`. A decide with one question.

`on` rendered as text against the run, compared byte-exact to each
case's value; `otherwise` when none matches.

The Decision-Making Agent reads `state` rendered against the run and
picks one of `options` by what each means; `otherwise` when it is not
sure enough, or gives no answer that holds to the decision contract.
Naming the step *is* switching the Decision-Making Agent on for it.

min_confidence.description:
How sure the pick must be to be taken; the node's
`decisions.confidence.act` when absent.

oneOf.description:
Every flow out of it at once: done on entry, each unlabelled flow
taken. Where the branches meet, the step they flow into joins them.

`items` renders to a JSON array; one `each` per item, the body flows
back into this step, then `done`.

`loop` while `when` holds — tested on every entry, the first included
— then `done`.

Call one operation of an outside platform through a connector
installed here. The connector is named by slug and the operation by
id, so the step reads the same on every node; the account — this
machine's way in — is the connector's default, a fixed id, or an
input of kind `account`. Every parameter is a template over the run,
rendered as text; the operation's own parameter kinds type it. The
output is what the operation selects from the answer, checked against
`output_schema` when one is declared.
The connector and the operation are absent while the designer has
not chosen them — a reference is a real id or absent, never an empty
string — and the validator says so (`ProblemKind::Unfilled`).

unattended.description:
The person's word that this write runs with nobody's approval
before it. A step calling an operation that `writes` needs an
`approval` or `human` step upstream, or this — never silence
(`ProblemKind::UngatedWrite`). Meaningless on a read.

oneOf.description:
Hold until the world moves: a delay, a moment, a schedule, a named
signal, a message, a project's change, a run's end, a platform topic,
or a person releasing it.

Raise a named signal — heard by `signal` starts, waits and boundary
events — with a payload of templates rendered against the run. Its
output is `{ signal }`.

Post into a conversation as an agent — `author`, or the Workflow
Agent when none is named. Mentions wake the addressed agents; none
wakes nobody.

author.description:
Whose message it is. Must resolve to an agent — never a person
or a team; absent, the Workflow Agent speaks.

oneOf.description: A sub-goal with its own workflow, `refines`-linked to this one.

inputs.description:
What the child's run is given: an input of its workflow to the
template that says it, rendered against this run and read by the
kind the child's input declares. A spawn is a start by hand made
by a step, so what the child's start asks for, the step gives —
every input it requires and no default fills.

wait.description: Wait for the child's run to finish before this step completes.

oneOf.description:
An end event. `finish = "path"` (the default) ends this path — the
run is done once every path has drained, as after a step with no
`then`; `"done"` finishes the run now, cancelling what is still live;
`"failed"` fails this step and the run now.

Step.description:
One node of the graph.

Deserialization refuses a key it does not know, for the step's own fields
and for the kind's ([`StepKind::fields_of`]): `retires = 2` is an error,
not a step that never retries. The kind is flattened beside `id` and
`name`, which is why the check is written by hand.

oneOf.description:
A person, by hand: *Run…*, a goal's start, `bisa workflow run`,
`POST /workflows/{id}/runs`. Maps nothing and has no guard.

On a cadence: `every` so many seconds, or at each `cron` occurrence in
`tz`.

A call to the node: local under the control-plane token, and public —
secret-authenticated from outside — only when `public` is set and the
machine allows public hooks (`events.public_hooks`).
A message posted into a conversation.

in.description:
The conversation it lands in — a channel id, a direct channel's, a
conversation's or a goal's thread (a template); absent, anywhere.

mentions.description: It mentions this agent, team or person.

contains.description: Its text contains this, case-insensitively (a template).

oneOf.description:
A named signal, raised by an `emit` step, a session, a person or an
A2A task.

name.description: The signal's name (a template).

oneOf.description:
A change in one project: a commit, a push or fetch, a pull request, a
merge, files.

project.description: Absent while the designer has not chosen one: a problem, never `""`.

glob.description: Only files matching this (`*` and `?`), for `files` (a template).

oneOf.description: A run that ended — of one workflow or of any.
One of the engine's own bus events, by topic — the advanced door.

fields.description: Exact matches on the event's own fields (templates).

params.description: The operation's parameters, as templates over the listening inputs.

oneOf.description:
An outside platform, polled through one of a connector's **read**
operations: every item its answer lists that an earlier poll did not
is one occurrence. `key` is the dotted path, inside one item, of the
field that tells items apart; the first poll only learns what is there.
The connector and the operation are absent while the designer has not
chosen them — never an empty string.

A shell command on a cadence — `sh -c {inputs.command}` — judged by the
command guard like a `check` step, run in its project's tree or in its
own scratch folder; `fire_on` says which results begin a run.

StartOn.description:
What begins a run at a `start` step. Its fields are fixed values,
`{inputs.<name>}` templates or `{ input = … }` references over the inputs
the host listens with — resolved when the start is armed
([`StartOn::resolve`]), so one template serves every workspace.

uint64OrInput.description:
Either a fixed value or the name of an input that carries it.

The schema is named after what it carries (`AssigneeOrInput`,
`uint64OrInput`): one name for every instantiation would leave the
generator to number them, and a number moves when the schema's order does.

stringOrInput.description:
Either a fixed value or the name of an input that carries it.

The schema is named after what it carries (`AssigneeOrInput`,
`uint64OrInput`): one name for every instantiation would leave the
generator to number them, and a number moves when the schema's order does.

MessageFrom.description: who wrote a message: `you`, `agents`, or one agent, person or team — or an input of kind `assignee` naming one

AssigneeOrInput.description:
Either a fixed value or the name of an input that carries it.

The schema is named after what it carries (`AssigneeOrInput`,
`uint64OrInput`): one name for every instantiation would leave the
generator to number them, and a number moves when the schema's order does.

ProjectIdOrInput.description:
Either a fixed value or the name of an input that carries it.

The schema is named after what it carries (`AssigneeOrInput`,
`uint64OrInput`): one name for every instantiation would leave the
generator to number them, and a number moves when the schema's order does.

oneOf.description: A branch head moved — a commit, whoever made it.
A remote-tracking branch moved: this machine pushed or fetched.
A pull request the platform's workstreams opened or adopted changed.
One of those pull requests was merged.
Files in the tree changed.

RunEnd.description: How a run ended, as a run event hears it.

OperationId.description: A operation id: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', '.', ':'

AccountIdOrInput.description:
Either a fixed value or the name of an input that carries it.

The schema is named after what it carries (`AssigneeOrInput`,
`uint64OrInput`): one name for every instantiation would leave the
generator to number them, and a number moves when the schema's order does.

oneOf.description:
The first failing result after a passing one — or after turning on:
the alert, once per outage.
Every failing result.
Every passing result.
Every result.

FireOn.description: Which results of a check start begin a run.

debounce_secs.description:
Drop an occurrence within this many seconds of the last run this
listener started.

Guard.description:
Rate and overlap controls, applied by the runtime before a run starts, not
by the workflow.

oneOf.description: One run at a time; later occurrences wait in the durable backlog.
Dropped while the listener's last run is unfinished — and it says so.
Up to this many at once; the rest wait. `{ parallel = 4 }`.

Overlap.description:
What an occurrence does while runs of its listener are still live —
counted over live runs, never over dispatches.

EffortChoice.description: What somebody asks for: a level, or `auto`.

oneOf.description: Reads state, no side effects.
Mutates files inside the work-item's workspace.
Arbitrary execution or effects outside the workspace.

ToolTier.description:
Risk tier of a tool action. Unknown or malformed tool names classify as
`Exec` — the safe default (omp's approval-mode rule).

id.description: Stable token. Answers name this, never the label.

detail.description: One line of "what this actually costs you", shown under the label.

recommended.description:
The asker's own recommendation. At most one option per question may
set it — two recommendations is not advice.

AskOption.description:
One offered answer to a question.

`id` is the token the human's answer comes back as; `label` is what they
read. They are separate so that rewording a question after it was asked
cannot change what a recorded answer meant.

oneOf.description: Exit 0 in the goal's placement is a pass.

An upstream step's output must satisfy this JSON Schema. The step is
absent while the designer has not chosen one (`ProblemKind::Unfilled`).
A `human` step's answer selected this option.

A `check` or `approval` step passed (`Done`) or did not (`Failed`,
or diverted by one of its boundary events).

Hour-of-day window, inclusive, in UTC. `from_hour > to_hour` wraps
midnight (22..6 is "overnight").
Every condition in `of` holds. Empty holds.
At least one condition in `of` holds. Empty does not.
Exactly one condition in `of` holds. Empty does not.
The condition does not hold.

Condition.description:
A rule's test. A **closed, typed set**, deliberately not an expression
language: an evaluator would make every workflow a scripting surface
running unreviewed on the node's own privileges, and it would be untestable
without I/O. Six leaves and four combinators (`all`, `any`, `one`,
`not`) that nest to [`Condition::MAX_DEPTH`]; another case is a code
change with a test, which is the point. No leaf reads the event that
began the run: a start's input mapping turns it into typed inputs, and a
rule reads those.

Branch.description:
A branch label on a `decide` step and on the flows leaving it. Compared
byte-exact.

oneOf.description: The first rule that holds: one branch.
Every rule that holds: as many branches as hold, all at once.

Case.description:
One case of a `switch`: the value the rendered subject must equal, and
the branch that takes.

JudgeOption.description:
One option of a `judge`: the branch it takes, and what choosing it means —
the sentence the Decision-Making Agent reads.

oneOf.description:
Seconds from the moment the step is entered — fixed, or read from a
`number` input so one template serves many holds.

A moment: `at` renders against the run to Unix seconds or an RFC 3339
timestamp — a deadline an input or an upstream step names.

The next occurrence of a cron expression — fixed, or read from a
`text` input.
A named signal whose payload carries every field, exactly.

name.description: The signal's name (a template).

oneOf.description: A message posted into a conversation.

in.description:
The conversation it lands in — a channel id, a direct channel's, a
conversation's or a goal's thread (a template); absent, anywhere.

mentions.description: It mentions this agent, team or person.

contains.description: Its text contains this, case-insensitively (a template).

oneOf.description: A change in one project.

project.description: Absent while the designer has not chosen one: a problem, never `""`.

glob.description: Only files matching this (`*` and `?`), for `files` (a template).

oneOf.description: A run that ended.
One of the engine's own bus events.

fields.description: Exact matches on the event's own fields (templates).

oneOf.description:
A person releases it — or a call does (`POST …/release`), with a
payload that becomes the step's output.

WaitFor.description:
What a `wait` holds for — a catch event. Its filters are the start
events' types ([`crate::listen`]), their fields rendered against the run.

oneOf.description: This path: the run is done once every path has drained.
The run, now: done, and whatever is still live is cancelled.
The run, now: this step fails, and the run with it.

Flow.description:
A directed edge. Deserializes from a bare `"step-id"` as well as from the
object, so a template can write `then = ["build"]`.

name.description:
Unique among the step's boundaries and branches; a divert's flows are
labelled with it.

oneOf.description: Stop the step and take the flows labelled with the boundary's name.

Post into a conversation beside the live step, as a `notify` step
does: into `scope` (the run's own conversation when absent), as
`author` (the Workflow Agent when absent).
Raise a named signal beside the live step, as an `emit` step does.

Boundary.description:
One boundary event of a step. The act sits flattened beside `name` and
`on`: `{ name = "late", on = { event = "after", secs = 172800 }, act =
"divert" }`.

oneOf.description:
Once, this many seconds after the step was entered — fixed, or read
from a `number` input.

Every this many seconds after the step was entered, at most `max`
times: a reminder. Never a divert.

A message posted into a conversation, filtered as a message start is —
its fields render against the run.

in.description:
The conversation it lands in — a channel id, a direct channel's, a
conversation's or a goal's thread (a template); absent, anywhere.

mentions.description: It mentions this agent, team or person.

contains.description: Its text contains this, case-insensitively (a template).

oneOf.description: A named signal with exact fields.

name.description: The signal's name (a template).

BoundaryOn.description: What a boundary listens for while its step is live.

oneOf.description: Every incoming flow that can still arrive has arrived or died.
The first arrival is enough.

Exactly one incoming flow arrives once every one that could has
settled; two is a failure of the step (an exclusive-or at fan-in).
The run fails.
Continue along the unlabelled flows as if the step were done.
Continue at one named step and nowhere else.

Point.description:
A place on the designer's canvas: whole pixels, as the canvas snaps them,
so the same picture is the same numbers wherever it is drawn.

oneOf.description: `agent:<id>`, `team:<id>` or `human:<hex>`, in wire form.
A project id.

An account of one connector, by id — this machine's way into an
outside platform, which a template cannot know. The connector is
absent while the designer has not chosen one: a problem
(`ProblemKind::Unfilled`), never a refusal.

One way a run begins: by hand, or on an event ([`StartOn`]). Done the
moment the run enters it. Several are several ways in: a run enters
the one it began at and the others are skipped. `inputs` maps the
event onto the run's inputs — templates reading `{event.<path>}` and
nothing else, the one place the event is read — and `guard` says what
an occurrence does while runs it started are still live. A `manual`
start maps nothing and has no guard.

model.description:
A model pin for this step's sessions. **Never substituted**: an
unavailable pin fails the step rather than running something the
author did not ask for. Absent means the agent's own plan.

effort.description:
An effort pin for this step's sessions: a level, or `auto` for
the Decision-Making Agent to name one. It wins over the model's
own and the agent's plan, and is then clamped to what the harness
and the model take. Absent means the agent's own.

oneOf.description:
A work item run by an agent: the existing executor, placement and
harness walk. Completes when the item yields a result.

A person answers — from the options offered, in free text, or "not
sure" — or does something by hand and marks the step done.

A signed decision under the workspace's `approval` policy. Declined is
a failure of the step.

Pass or fail, judged by a command or by a schema over an upstream
output. A check that does not pass is a failure of the step.

`pick = "first"` (the default): the first rule whose condition holds
names the branch. `pick = "every"`: every rule that holds does, and
their flows are all taken at once. `otherwise` when none holds. Only
the chosen branches' flows are taken.
`yes` when `when` holds, else `no`. A decide with one question.

`on` rendered as text against the run, compared byte-exact to each
case's value; `otherwise` when none matches.

min_confidence.description:
How sure the pick must be to be taken; the node's
`decisions.confidence.act` when absent.

oneOf.description:
The Decision-Making Agent reads `state` rendered against the run and
picks one of `options` by what each means; `otherwise` when it is not
sure enough, or gives no answer that holds to the decision contract.
Naming the step *is* switching the Decision-Making Agent on for it.

Every flow out of it at once: done on entry, each unlabelled flow
taken. Where the branches meet, the step they flow into joins them.

`items` renders to a JSON array; one `each` per item, the body flows
back into this step, then `done`.

`loop` while `when` holds — tested on every entry, the first included
— then `done`.

unattended.description:
The person's word that this write runs with nobody's approval
before it. A step calling an operation that `writes` needs an
`approval` or `human` step upstream, or this — never silence
(`ProblemKind::UngatedWrite`). Meaningless on a read.

oneOf.description:
Call one operation of an outside platform through a connector
installed here. The connector is named by slug and the operation by
id, so the step reads the same on every node; the account — this
machine's way in — is the connector's default, a fixed id, or an
input of kind `account`. Every parameter is a template over the run,
rendered as text; the operation's own parameter kinds type it. The
output is what the operation selects from the answer, checked against
`output_schema` when one is declared.
The connector and the operation are absent while the designer has
not chosen them — a reference is a real id or absent, never an empty
string — and the validator says so (`ProblemKind::Unfilled`).

Hold until the world moves: a delay, a moment, a schedule, a named
signal, a message, a project's change, a run's end, a platform topic,
or a person releasing it.

Raise a named signal — heard by `signal` starts, waits and boundary
events — with a payload of templates rendered against the run. Its
output is `{ signal }`.

author.description:
Whose message it is. Must resolve to an agent — never a person
or a team; absent, the Workflow Agent speaks.

oneOf.description:
Post into a conversation as an agent — `author`, or the Workflow
Agent when none is named. Mentions wake the addressed agents; none
wakes nobody.

inputs.description:
What the child's run is given: an input of its workflow to the
template that says it, rendered against this run and read by the
kind the child's input declares. A spawn is a start by hand made
by a step, so what the child's start asks for, the step gives —
every input it requires and no default fills.

wait.description: Wait for the child's run to finish before this step completes.

oneOf.description: A sub-goal with its own workflow, `refines`-linked to this one.

An end event. `finish = "path"` (the default) ends this path — the
run is done once every path has drained, as after a step with no
`then`; `"done"` finishes the run now, cancelling what is still live;
`"failed"` fails this step and the run now.

text.description:
The sentence, as data — a message of `locales/en/problems.ftl`
(`problem-<kind>-…`) with the step and input names as arguments.

Problem.description:
One thing wrong with a definition. The designer renders problems by kind
and selects the step; `Adopt` and `Start` refuse while any exists.

oneOf.description:
A condition nests deeper than [`Condition::MAX_DEPTH`], or an
`all`/`any`/`one` in it has nothing in it.
Nothing on a loop's body side flows back into it.
A loop's exit flow leads to a step that flows back into the loop.
A loop allows zero iterations.
A connector step names a connector that is not installed.
A connector step names an operation its connector does not have.
A connector step leaves out a parameter the operation requires.
A connector step names an account this node does not hold.

A `connector` step calls an operation that writes with no `approval`
or `human` step upstream and no `unattended: true` of its own — a
write nobody gated and nobody said they meant to leave ungated.

A step string reads `{params.…}` or `{account.…}`, which only a
connector definition may.

A choice not made yet: a connector step's connector or operation, a
schema check's step, an account input's connector. The designer
births these absent and fills them in the inspector; the checks that
depend on the choice wait for it.

A `notify` step's `author` is a person or a team; only an agent speaks
for a workflow.

A `{steps.x…}` placeholder, a condition or a schema check names an
ancestor that is not sure to have run when the step is entered: it
runs after the step on a loop's first pass, a branch or an `any`
join reaches the step without it, or it may have failed and been
passed over (`on_fail` skip or then).

Reading the output of a kind that yields none, a `human`'s output
rather than its answer, or the answer of a step that is not `human`.

`{steps.x.output.<field>}` or a rule's path whose first segment the
producer does not promise: not in its `output_schema`'s `required`,
nothing at all without a schema, or a key a fixed-shape kind never
writes.

A step reads `{goal.statement}` or `{goal.title}` in a run of the
workspace, which has no goal to read — never a problem of the
definition, only of where it is started ([`Workflow::scope_problems`]).

A `start` step has a flow or a fail route into it: a start begins a
run and nothing inside one leads back to it.
More than one `manual` start: a run by hand begins at exactly one.

A `manual` start carries an input mapping or a guard — what only an
event start reads.

The event read anywhere but a start's input mapping, or a start's
mapping or event fields reading a root that is not theirs.

Boundary events on a step whose work cannot be stopped while it is
live ([`may_carry_boundaries`]).

A reminder (`every`) that diverts: it would stop the step at its first
tick.

A clock that cannot run: zero seconds, a reminder that fires no
times, a schedule that is both `every` and `cron`, or neither.
A signal's name that is not dotted lowercase words.

A connector start that cannot poll: an operation that writes, one that
takes a file, or no `key` to tell items apart.

A `platform` start or wait naming no topic, or one the engine never
emits.

A `spawn` naming a workflow only events start: nothing can run it by
hand.

An agent step pins an effort and none of the harnesses it names has
the effort control: the pin would be sent to nobody.

A `spawn` that gives its workflow an input it does not declare, or
leaves out one it requires and no default fills: the child's run
could never start.

id.description: The message id, as `locales/<lang>/*.ftl` spells it: kebab-case, area-prefixed.

args.description: The arguments, by the names the message's `{ $name }` placeables use.

Text.description:
A message of the catalog with its arguments — the platform's sentence,
not yet in any language.

anyOf.description: A whole number — a count a message may select a plural on.
A string: an id, a name, a path — the world's word, shown as it is.

scope.description: What the run is for. Set when it is made; a run never changes scope.

workflow.description: Frozen at start; replaced only by [`RunEvent::Amended`].

start.description:
The start step the run begins at. `None` for a run by hand while it is
queued — it begins at the manual entry, and [`RunEvent::Start`] writes
which step that was.

event.description:
The occurrence that began this run, whole — or a test run's sample —
when an event did. Its start's input mapping read it; no step does.

dispatched.description:
The id of the queued signal this run was dispatched from: one signal,
one run, even across a crash between the two. A restart keeps the
event and never this.

chain.description:
The listeners the causal line behind this run passed through: its
event's chain, widened by every chained event it hears — what keeps
a signal it raises from starting its own listener again.

queued_at.description: When the run was made. The queue's order is `(queued_at, id)`.

started_at.description: When [`RunEvent::Start`] was applied; `None` while the run is queued.

cancelled.description: Why the run was cancelled, when it was. A cancelled run has no outcome.

seq.description:
Orders step settlements: every accepted event **and every change to a
step's record** advances it, and the record stamps it. The machine
tells a flow that arrived *after* a step last finished from one that
arrived before — the loop case — without trusting a clock. Per change,
not per event, because one event settles a whole chain: a `decide`
that finishes in the same pass as the step it loops back into must
still read as *later* than that step.

revision.description: Snapshot authority, bumped by the store on every write.

WorkflowRun.description:
The addressable `kind:33413` snapshot, filed in its home's `state/`: its
goal's, or its own folder's for a run of the workspace
([`WorkflowRun::home`]).

oneOf.description:
A run of the workspace: started from its workflow — *Run…*,
`bisa workflow run`, one of its start events while it is On — at once,
beside any other. Its ceiling is frozen when it is made: the listening
budget, else the workspace default (`budget.default.*`); unlimited is
none of the three.
A goal's run: one live at a time, the rest queued behind it.

RunScope.description:
What a run is for — the workspace itself, or a goal. The two differ in
three ways and in nothing else the machine decides: a goal's runs take
turns (one live, the rest queued) while the workspace's all start at
once; a goal carries the budget its runs spend against while a run of the
workspace carries its own; and a goal is the home a goal's run is filed
under while a run of the workspace is its own ([`WorkflowRun::home`]).

listener.description:
The listener it was raised for; `None` for a named signal recorded
only so a re-armed `wait` can replay it.

name.description: A named signal's name, or a platform topic.

chain.description: The listeners the causal line behind this occurrence passed through.

dedupe_key.description: What makes a second write of the same occurrence one signal.

SignalSource.description:
What kind of event a signal records — the start events' words, and
`test` for a run a person started as if an event had happened.

SignalScope.description:
Where a heard event belongs: the whole workspace, or one goal. A goal's
run raises its signals on its goal.

Chain.description:
The listeners one causal line of events passed through, oldest first,
and how many hops deep it is.

spent.description:
The step was entered once more than its `max_visits` allows, and
failed for it. A spent step takes no further arrival — a flow into it
is dropped — so a ring whose steps pass over their own failures ends.
Its visits come back with a loop's next iteration, which starts its
body's count afresh, and with an amendment that raises the bound.

attempts.description: Failed attempts in the current visit.

seq.description: The run's `seq` when this record last changed state.

entered.description:
The run's `seq` when the step was last entered. What tells an `any`
join a fresh round from the slower arm of the one it already took:
a source entered after the join last changed is new; one entered
before it is the same fan-out arriving late.

gate.description: The decision that completed an `approval` step.

cursor.description:
Where a `for_each` or a `while` stands between iterations; `None`
outside a loop. The one field an entry does not reset — save an
entry from outside the loop's body, which starts afresh.

fired.description:
The boundary events that fired during this visit, by name: how many
times, and when last. A reminder re-arms from here — never more than
its `max`, across restarts — and an entry resets it.

StepRecord.description: What has happened to one step in this run.

oneOf.description:
Finished. A gateway names the branches it chose — one, or every one
that held — and its labelled flows with those names are taken; with
none named, the unlabelled flows are.

Stopped by the boundary event `by`: its work was cancelled, and only
the flows labelled `by` are taken.

selected.description: Option ids chosen. Empty when the question offered none.

text.description: What they typed — alongside the options, not instead of them.

unsure.description: They do not know. Not a decline.

Answer.description: What a human said back. One value that can say all three things at once.

items.description:
The array `items` rendered to, parsed once when the loop started;
`None` for a `while`.

index.description: Iterations dispatched so far — the index of the next one.

LoopCursor.description: A loop kind's place in its iterations.

seq.description: The run's `seq` at the last fire.

Fired.description: One boundary event's fires in the current visit of its step.

oneOf.description:
A person stopped it: a goal's live run, its queue withdrawn with it
(the goal stays open, ready for a new run), or one run of the
workspace.

A person restarted it: this run ended and a new run of the same
workflow and inputs started in its place — ahead of a goal's queue,
or beside the workspace's other runs.
A person took this run out of its goal's queue before it started.

The goal was closed while this run was live or queued. Nested rather
than flattened: a flattened tagged enum inside a tagged enum is a
schema the desktop's type generator cannot read.

Its workflow was archived or deleted while this run of the workspace
went: retiring a workflow retires its runs first.

CancelCause.description:
Why a run was cancelled. The one word the run keeps, the journal
records and every screen prints; a `ClosureReason` is the goal's.

oneOf.description: Given up on. No further work will be done.
Replaced by another goal, which is named.

Home.description:
The record whose folder files a run's truth: its goal, or — for a run of
the workspace — the run itself. Recorded nowhere as a choice: a run's
home follows from its scope ([`crate::WorkflowRun::home`]).

oneOf.description: The engine bound a work item to a running `agent` step.

The step failed and **must not be tried again**, whatever its
`retries`: a `connector` write that may already have reached the
platform — a timeout, a lost answer, a 5xx after sending — with no
idempotency key to make a resend safe. The step fails at once and
`on_fail` decides; the reason tells the person to look at the
platform before running it again.

A restart found the step live with nothing behind it: the session,
the command, the call or the post died with the last process. Not a
failure of the step's own — `attempts` is untouched — and what
follows is the kind's: an `agent` resumes on the work item it already
has, a `check` runs again, the rest run again only within their
`retries` and fail otherwise.

A `wait` heard what it waits for — a named signal, a message, a
project's change, a run's end, a platform topic. The payload is the
step's output; the chain behind it widens the run's.
A `wait`'s delay, moment or schedule came due.

A person — or a call — released a `wait` or a `spawn` that waits; a
payload, when given, is the step's output.

One of a live step's boundary events fired, for the visit that began
at `entered` (the step record's `entered`): a divert stops the step, an
act runs beside it. A fire for an earlier visit is stale and refused.
Replace the steps that have not started.

End the run for the cause named: every live step is cancelled and
the run is finished. Accepted on a queued run too, where nothing is
live and the only effect is [`RunEffect::Cancelled`].

RunEvent.description:
The only way a run changes. Constructing one is the proof the move exists;
`apply` decides whether it is legal *here*.

ApprovalId.description:
The journal event id of the signed `kind:3401` decision that authorises a
gated move. Carried on the [`crate::run::RunEvent::Decided`] that an
`approval` step completes with, so the run and the decision that moved it
are joined by an id and not by trust.

oneOf.description: Finished, naming the branches a gateway chose.
Stopped by a boundary event that diverts.

A boundary event that does not divert acted beside the live step: a
post, or a signal.
Made behind its goal's live run; it starts when its turn comes.

Started — at once when made on an idle goal or in the workspace, or
from a goal's queue — at `start`, on the signal `signal` when an event
began it.

Retirement.description:
`GET /goals/{id}/retirement` and `GET /workflows/{wfid}/retirement`: what
retiring would touch, for the person to weigh — the goal's run that is
going, a workflow's runs of the workspace that are going (retired with
it) and how many it has in all (kept under an archived workflow, gone
with a deleted one), the agent sessions aborted and the harnesses
terminated, the refusal a deletion would meet, the designs that go or
stay, what still uses a workflow, the projects born of the thing with
what each holds (their workstreams by id, so the desktop can count its
own terminals there), the projects merely attached.

SettingOrigin.description: Where a resolved value came from.

ResolvedSetting.description: A resolved setting: its value and the scope it came from.

name.description: The effective `user.name`, whatever layer it comes from.

global.description:
The global pair, when there is one — offered so a person can pin it to
this repository.

profile.description:
The profile the effective identity came from (ide/04 §Profiles by
organization), when it came from one; the `source` reads `global` then,
since the value resolves outside the repository.

suggested.description:
What this repository could commit as, when nobody is set: the identity
the checkout's connected code host account suggests — offered for one
click, never written by itself. `null` with an identity, without an
account, or when the host gives nothing to build an email from.

GitIdentityView.description:
`GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/identity` — who authors commits in this
checkout's repository, and where that answer comes from. A worktree shares
its repository's config, so every workstream of a project answers alike.

oneOf.description: Both keys are set in the repository itself.
Both resolve from outside the repository — the global config, in practice.
A commit here would fail.

IdentitySource.description: Where a repository's commit identity comes from (`bisa_vcs::IdentitySource`).

GitIdent.description:
A committer as the wire spells it: `{name, email}` — what an identity's
view answers. Who commits is *written* as two keys of the repository's
local config (`PUT /workstreams/{wid}/git/config`, `user.name` and
`user.email`, never global); a creation body carries the same two keys
inside its `git_config` map.

CommitterSuggestionView.description: A committer a code host account suggests, and whose account it is.

global.description: The person's global git pair, when both keys are set. Read, never written here.

pending.description: Projects nobody has said who commits in yet.

CommitterView.description:
`GET /git/committer` — what the ask dialog seeds from: the
person's global git pair and the projects still asking who commits.

workstream.description: The primary workstream — where `PUT …/git/config` writes the answer.

origin.description: Where the project was born — the dialog's first sentence says it.

global.description: The person's global git pair, when both keys are set.

PendingCommitterView.description:
One project still asking who commits — the facts the `committer_needed`
frame carries, so a dialog seeded here shows what one that heard the
frame shows.

oneOf.description: Just created; nothing resolved.
A person's commit was refused.
An agent's settlement commit was refused; it is made once an identity is set.
Found at a start with no identity resolving in it.

HarnessUsage.description:
`GET /harnesses/{id}/usage` — what a harness's account has left, as the
harness's own source reports it, or why there is no report. Never a
credential: percentages, labels, reset times, a plan's word.

oneOf.description: The report.
This harness reports no usage limits; `reason` is its own sentence.
The harness could report, but is not signed in here.
Reads are off — `harness.usage.reads` — so nothing was asked.
The read failed; `reason` never quotes what came back.

UsageState.description: What asking a harness for its usage answered.

read_at.description: Unix seconds the report was read.

windows.description: The limit windows, in the harness's order — the short one first.

extras.description: Beyond the windows: an extra-usage or credit balance, when reported.

UsageReport.description: One harness account's usage, read at one moment.

oneOf.description: The provider's usage endpoint, with the harness's own sign-in.

(its local `codehost.account`), or `null` to unpin it.

SshTest.description:
`POST /git/ssh/test` — one handshake with a git host: `user@host`, with
`key` when a profile's key should be the one offered.

scopes.description: The scopes that may hold a value: `machine`, `workspace`, `project`.

label.description: The label, in the request's language.

help.description: The sentence under the label, in the request's language; empty when the key has none.

SettingDef.description:
One registry entry, for a panel generated from the registry rather than
written by hand (`GET /settings/registry`). Its `label` and `help` are the
catalog's message `setting-<key>` in the request's language
(17 — Internationalisation); the registry itself carries no words.

SettingKind.description: What a setting may hold — the registry's `Kind`, on the wire.

value.description: The value, as the registry and a write spell it.

label.description: The value's word in the request's language (`setting-<key>.choice-<value>`).

SettingChoice.description: One value a `Choice` setting may take: the word stored, and the word shown.

SettingsWrite.description: `PUT /settings/{scope}`: the keys to write at that scope.

oneOf.description: The proxy the node's own environment names, if any.
No proxy, whatever the environment says.
The two URLs and the bypass list.

problems.description: What keeps the settings from being in force, if anything.

NetworkStatus.description: The `network.*` settings as the panel reads them, with what is in force.

oneOf.description: Every call leaves directly.

Calls leave through a proxy; the URLs masked, the bypass as the
tools read it.

ProxyEnvironment.description:
What the node's own process environment names, masked — the answer to
*what does `environment` mean here*.

ok.description: An answer came back — whatever its status; a 403 still proves the way.

via_proxy.description: Whether the request went through a proxy the policy names.

NetworkCheck.description: One request the person asked for, to see whether the way out works.

NetworkCheckRequest.description: `POST /network/check`: the URL to reach once through the outbound client.

text.description: The text, when the file is text and within the cap.

hash.description: sha256 of the served bytes — the `base_hash` a save must carry.

editable.description: Within the editable size; above it the client opens read-only.

truncated.description: Either side was cut at the cap.

FileSides.description:
`GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/sides?path=&staged=` — the two whole texts
of one file's change, for a comparison (ide/04 §The Changes view): the
index against the working tree, or HEAD against the index. A side git
does not hold — a new file's left, a deleted file's right — is `null`;
a binary side says so and carries no text; a side over the cap is cut
on a line and says `truncated`.

CommitFileDiff.description:
`GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/commit/{sha}/diff?path=` — one file's patch
in one commit, against the first parent (ide/05): the *Hunks* view of a
commit's file. Cut at 2 MiB on a line, `truncated` says so.

truncated.description: Either side was cut at the cap.

CommitFileSides.description:
`GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/commit/{sha}/sides?path=` — the two whole
texts of one file's change in one commit, for a comparison (ide/05): the
file as the first parent held it — at its old path for a rename — against
the file as the commit holds it. A side that is not there — a root
commit's or a new file's left, a deleted file's right — is `null`; a
binary side says so and carries no text; a side over the cap is cut on a
line and says `truncated`. The same shape as `FileSides` past the keys,
so one reader draws both.

truncated.description: A side was cut at the cap.

GitConflict.description:
`GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/conflict?path=`: a conflicted path whole —
its kind, its three sides from the index's stages (git's words: `ours`
is the current branch, under a rebase the branch rebased onto), and the
file as git wrote it on disk with its markers, for the block-by-block
resolution; `hash` guards the save that follows. A side that is not
there — deleted by one side, no base for a file added on both — is
`null`; `binary` when any side or the file is not text.

GitConflictKind.description: What kind of conflict an unmerged path is (`bisa_vcs::ConflictKind`).

branch.description: The branch the operation is on — under a rebase, the branch replayed.

GitOperationFacts.description:
`GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/operation`: the operation git has left
half-done, as facts read from its directory — so one started in a
terminal is described as well as one started here. `ours` and `theirs`
are git's: under a rebase `ours` is the branch rebased onto, `theirs`
the commit replayed. The desktop turns them into *mine* and *theirs*
once (`conflictSidesModel`).

GitInProgress.description:
The operation git has left half-done in a checkout, on the wire — what a
status reports, and what a client sends back to abort, continue or skip.

name.description: The branch or remote-tracking branch, when the side is one.

commit.description: The commit's full sha, when known.

subject.description: The commit's subject line, when known.

GitSideRef.description: One side of a half-done operation, named as far as git can name it.

GitSideRole.description: What a side of a half-done operation is (`bisa_vcs::SideRole`).

GitStep.description:
Where a rebase, pick or revert of several commits stands: the step git
stopped on, one-based, of the total.

GitMergePreview.description:
`GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/merge-preview?source=`: what merging
`source` into HEAD would do, before anything moves — `supported` is
false on a git without `merge-tree --write-tree`, and then nothing is
foreseen.

base_hash.description: Absent means create — refused if the path exists.

IdeDeleteEntry.description:
One entry of a batch delete: its path, and whether a folder's delete was
confirmed — what the confirmation shown for it records, entry by entry.

GitHunkApply.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/hunk` — one hunk, or the lines of one a person
picked, as a unified diff. `reverse` takes it back out of the index.

track.description: Follow `start` — a remote branch — as the upstream (`--track`).

switch.description: Check the new branch out too. That half is consented.

upstream.description: The remote branch to follow — `origin/main` — or null for none.

GitRebase.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/rebase`: the current branch replayed onto
`upstream` — or, with `onto`, only its commits since `upstream` replayed
onto `onto` — the dirty tree carried across with `autostash`.

GitRebasePlan.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/rebase/plan`: an interactive rebase planned
in full — every commit since `upstream`, oldest first, each with its action.

GitRebaseStep.description:
One step of an interactive rebase: the commit, its action, and — for a
reword or a squash the person wrote words for — the message.

GitRebaseAction.description: What happens to one commit of an interactive rebase.

message.description: The merge commit's message, when there is one to make.

GitMergeMode.description:
How a merge lands: git's default (a fast-forward when it can), always a
merge commit, a fast-forward or a refusal, or every change squashed into
the index for one commit of the person's.

no_commit.description: Leave the change staged for one commit of the person's.

mainline.description: The parent a merge commit is picked against (`-m`, 1-based).
The parent a merge commit is reverted against (`-m`, 1-based).

GitRevert.description: `POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/revert`: the commits to undo, oldest first.

message.description: The commit's message, replacing its own.

paths.description:
Staged first, then folded in. **Empty means "what is already
staged"**, never "everything" — the same rule as a commit's.

GitAmend.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/amend`: the last commit rewritten with what
is staged and this message.

GitOperation.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/abort`, `…/continue`, `…/skip`: the
operation half-done, by the same word a status reports it with.

take.description:
How the path is settled whole, by git; absent, the merged text
already saved is staged (index only).

GitResolve.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/resolve` — a conflicted path settled: with a
`side`, that side is taken whole (consented — the tree moves); without,
the merged text the person saved is staged, which is *Mark resolved*.

GitResolution.description:
How a conflicted path is settled whole, in git's words: `ours` is the
branch the operation runs on — during a rebase, the branch rebased onto
— `theirs` the other side; `delete` removes the path, the answer to a
side that deleted it.

patch.description: One hunk of the *unstaged* patch, reversed onto the tree.

paths.description: Whole paths, restored from the index.

ref.description: The full recovery ref name, as `GET …/git/recovery` listed it.

branch.description: The branch HEAD was on, when it was on one.

GitRecoveryRef.description:
One row of `GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/recovery` (ide/04): what a
consented operation saved before it ran, as `restore` wants it named.

SshNewKey.description:
A key pair to generate: its file name under the directory and the comment
the public key carries (an email, a machine — the person's word).

index.description:
Its position, newest first — what `stash@{n}` means right now. It
shifts under every push and drop, so a verb names `commit` too.

branch.description: The branch it was made on; `null` when HEAD was detached.

message.description: The message the person gave; `null` for git's own `WIP on …`.

GitStash.description:
One entry of `GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/stashes` (ide/04 §Stash): the
list is the repository's, shared by every worktree of the project.

include_untracked.description: Untracked files go too (`-u`; never ignored ones).

keep_index.description: The staged half stays staged in the tree as well (`--keep-index`).

paths.description: Only these paths; absent or empty is the whole tree.

GitStashTarget.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/stashes/{sha}/{apply|pop|drop}`: the index
the entry was listed at. The sha travels in the path; the two together
are the target, and a moved list is refused (`stash_moved`).

PrReview.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/pr/review`. `body` is the summary — required, in
words, for a `comment` or a `request_changes`; optional beside an `approve`.

ReviewComment.description:
One inline comment of a review. `line` is a line of the diff — a comment
on a line the pull request did not touch is refused by the code host —
and `start_line`/`start_side` make it a span ending at `line`.

Side.description:
Which side of the diff an inline comment sits on: the base (a deleted or
unchanged-on-the-left line) or the head (an added or unchanged line).

path.description: The document the request is about (decides the language, hence the server).

delete_branch.description:
Delete the head branch on the code host once the merge lands (the merge
dialog's toggle, defaulting from `git.delete_branch_after_merge`).

env_auto.description:
Whether the node's own environment is read for detectors, and how
many of its variables are armed — a count, never a name or a value.

content.description: The content screen's two words (11-security §What an agent reads from outside).

classifier_ready.description:
Whether the classifier's agent exists, is enabled and names a harness
this node can launch.

vault_size.description: How many secrets the vault holds right now — a count, never a value.

oneOf.description:
A regular expression. When it has a group named `secret`, that group
is the secret and the rest of the match stays; otherwise the whole
match is.

The value of one environment variable of the node's own process, read
when the redactor is built. The name is stored; the value never is.

RedactDetector.description: How a rule recognises a secret.

RuleOrigin.description: Where a rule came from — shipped with the platform or written by a person.

hint.description:
What a refusal by this rule adds after its label — the way the agent
should take instead, in a sentence it reads as the tool's answer.
Only a refusal carries it; an ask or a classify has nothing to add.

oneOf.description: Run it, without asking anyone.
Refuse it; the agent hears the reason.
Ask the person who owns the goal.

Ask the classifier first; harmful goes to the person (or is refused),
safe runs.

GuardAction.description: What a matching rule asks for.

oneOf.description: A regular expression over the shell command, whitespace-normalised.

A glob over every path-like argument, tried as written, as an absolute
path under the session's cwd, and as `~/…` when it is under the home.

An exact tool name — `Bash`, `Write`, `mcp__bisa__post_message` — or
a prefix ending in `*`: `mcp__gh__*` is every tool of one MCP
server, `mcp__*` every tool of every MCP server.
Every call.

rule.description: The rule's id, or `#<index>` when it could not even be read.

PolicyProblem.description: A rule the policy could not use, and why.

SecurityFeature.description: Which feature a problem belongs to.

harness.description:
The harness and the model that read when the provider is `harness`; an
empty model is the harness's own default.

effort.description:
How hard that model works on a reading: a level, never `auto`, fitted
at launch to what the model takes.

oneOf.description: The classifier agent, on its own harness and models.
One harness with one of its models, no agent in between.
The Decision-Making Agent, as the `decisions.*` settings set it up.

ClassifierProvider.description: Who reads a subject for the classifier.

Effort.description:
A level a model runs at, lowest first. The order is the enum's own, so
`Effort::Low < Effort::High`.

OnHarmful.description: What the classifier does with a harmful verdict.

ContentSettings.description:
The content screen's two words (11-security §What an agent reads from
outside): whether what an agent reads from outside is put to the
classifier first, and what a harmful reading does.

HarnessGuard.description: One harness's standing with the guard.

home.description: The goal, or the run of the workspace, the call was made for.

on_behalf_of.description: The person on another node the session was working for, when it was.

GuardDecision.description:
One decision the guard made, as the status route shows it — the subject is
redacted, so this is safe to hand to a screen.

oneOf.description: It ran (or may run) — with a restored input when a placeholder was in it.
Refused; the agent heard the reason.
Put to a person, in the Inbox.
A guard rule matched — a built-in or a person's.
The classifier read the redacted call.
A person answered in the Inbox.

The content screen read what an agent was about to read from outside
— a page, a review — through the classifier.

LiveRunId.description: A live harness session's handle: a ULID, minted per launch.

RedactPreview.description:
What a redaction of `text` would do — on a vault of its own, so a preview
never teaches the real vault a secret.

GuardPreview.description: What the rules alone say about a call — no classifier, no restore.

decision.description:
`allow`, `deny` or `ask`; absent when the guard has no opinion and the
harness's own prompt stands.

updated_input.description: The input to run with, when a placeholder was restored.

GuardReply.description: What the guard hook prints back to Claude Code.

owed.description:
Whether the pending changes are owed a word (`manual`) or will be
kept by the next message (`auto`).

ChangesView.description:
A conversation's changes as the pane draws them: the turns that changed
something, oldest first, and how many files wait for a word.

oneOf.description: Edits land and are owed a review; a command no rule decided is asked.

Edits land and commands run; the changes stay reviewable and are
kept when the person sends their next message.

The agent reads and replies with a plan; an edit is refused and a
command is asked.

ConversationMode.description:
How far an agent goes on its own in a conversation about a checkout.
The mode never loosens the Tool & Commands Guard, the Redactor or the
classifier: the rules come first in every mode, and the mode only says
what happens to a call no rule decided.

overlapped.description: Somebody else edited the agent's own lines: an Undo asks first.

added.description: Lines this turn added to and removed from the file.

ChangeKind.description: What a turn did to a file.

oneOf.description: Owed a word, or waiting for the next message to keep it.

Somebody else took it away — a discard in Git › Changes, a checkout —
before a word was said.

ChangeState.description: Where a turn's change to a file stands.

base_text.description: The file before the pending changes; empty for one the agent made.

disk_hash.description:
The hash of the disk these hunks were cut from — what a settle of one
hunk states, so a hunk is never settled against a file that moved.

FileReviewView.description: One file under review, as the editor's lens draws it.

id.description:
Stable while the hunk's own text is: settling another hunk of the
file does not rename this one.

Hunk.description:
One pending difference between a file's base and its disk: the lines it
replaces in each, and their text.

LineSpan.description: A run of lines: where it starts (0-based) and how many.

GitRecoveryKind.description:
What a recovery ref points at (`bisa_vcs::RecoveryKind`, mirrored):
a tip to check out, the saved index and tree to apply, or a dropped stash
entry to put back on the list.

Skipped.description: A file a settle left alone, and why — a sentence a person reads.

grantable.description:
Whether *for this conversation* is on offer: only for the mode's own
ask or the screen's, never a guard rule's.

ConversationAsk.description: An ask as the pane draws it. `question` is already redacted.

oneOf.description: The classifier was sure it is safe.
The person allowed it — once, or for the host in this conversation.
The screen is off: framed, read at once.
Denied by the policy or the person: the agent reads a sentence.

ContentVerdict.description: What became of one content, on the bus and in the framing.

oneOf.description: A tool call the guard put to the person.

Content from outside the screen held before the agent read it: where
it came from in words, its URL when it is a page, why it was held
(the classifier's sentence, or *no verdict*), and an excerpt — all
redacted already.

agent.description:
The Decision-Making Agent itself: its reserved id, its name, what it
is.

answers_as.description: The model that answers, as a record names it.

calibrated.description: Whether the provider's probabilities are a calibrated model's.

ready.description: Whether the provider can be asked as it is set up — and why not.

key_stored.description:
Whether an API key is stored for the provider; `None` for a provider

points.description: Every decision point, and whether the workspace's switch reaches it.

DeciderStatus.description: What Settings › Decision Making and `bisa decisions status` read.

default_provider.description: What answers out of the box, before any setting is written.

Whether a browser tab an agent opens needs a person watching.

A place in the platform where a judgement may stand in for a fixed rule.

`docs/architecture/15-decision-making-agent.md`.

Readiness.description: The five checks and whether every one is ready.

note.description: What the agent should do instead — it hears this as the reason.

ReadinessCheck.description: One check, in words a person acts on.

InstallHint.description:
How to install one thing: the official page, the install lines per
platform, how to check it landed, and how to sign in when the tool needs it.

PlatformCommand.description:
One install line for one platform. Written once, here, and only ever

oneOf.description: Not on this machine: install it.
Here, but not set up to work: configure it.

ReadinessDoor.description: Where the desktop takes the person to fix a check by hand.

effort.description:
How hard the plan's models work — a level, or `auto` — unless a model
states its own. Absent means the `agents.effort` setting.

default": `order` yields nothing and the caller pins no model.

suited_for.description:
What this model is the right one for, in a sentence — what `AutoRoute`

goal.description: The goal it was made on, when it was made on one.
