model.description: The model that answered, or the one that was asked when none did.

calibrated.description: Whether the probabilities are a calibrated model's.

questions.description:
The questions as they were asked — redacted, like the state they were

answers.description: Empty when the provider gave no answer that holds to the contract.

One judgement, as it is recorded: on a goal's journal, and in the node's

state.description: What is being judged: text, or any JSON a caller composed.

model.description: The model that answered, as the provider names it.

GuardHookRequest.description:

One script as a settings surface sees it: the text, and whether this

by_x.description: For `scroll`: how far, in pixels, when `to` is not given.

headless.description:
For `open`, the agent's word on whether the tab is kept out of sight;
absent, the workspace's policy decides (`headless_for`).

BrowserRequest.description:
One request, as the tool sent it and the desktop reads it. `target` is a
CSS selector or a ref a snapshot answered (`e12`).

ScriptPhase.description:
The three moments a lifecycle script runs, and the run command the IDE's
Terminal menu opens in a terminal.

BrowserReadFormat.description: How `browser_read` answers an element: its text, or its HTML.

BrowserScope.description:
Where the asking session works, decided here ([`home_of`]) — so the
desktop roots a tab it opens beside that screen: the checkout's IDE, the
goal, the channel, the direct message, the conversation; with none, the
workspace's own Browser pane.

BrowserHome.description: The screen a tab is at home beside, and which one.

BrowserHomeScope.description:
Where a tab is at home — the screens the desktop can show one beside,
word for word the desktop's `BROWSER_SCOPES`.

answer.description:
What the page was answered: nothing for an alert, `true` for a
confirm, the default text for a prompt.

BrowserDialog.description:
A dialog the page asked while the agent's request ran — answered for it,
and reported.

oneOf.description: The page's load to finish.
The element `target` names to be in the page.
`text` to be somewhere in the page's text.
The element `target` names to be gone from the page.
The page to stop changing for half a second.

BrowserConsoleLine.description: One line the page wrote to its console, or an error it raised.

BrowserTab.description: An open tab as the desktop lists it.

text.description:
The page's or the element's text, a find's matches, a snapshot's
outline — bounded.

navigated.description: The act moved the page: the answer is the page it moved to.

count.description: How many a find or a snapshot counted.

scroll.description: Where the page stands after a scroll.

dialogs.description: The dialogs the page asked since the last answer, each answered.

console.description: What the page wrote to its console.

screenshot.description:
A screenshot's PNG, uploaded to the workspace's attachments by the
desktop; the engine turns it into [`Self::path`].

path.description:
The screenshot's named copy on this machine — set by the engine, never
by the desktop, which names no path.

BrowserResult.description: What the desktop answers: `ok` with the facts, or a refusal in words.

BrowserScrollPosition.description: Where a page is scrolled to, and how big it is.

mergeable.description: `None` while the code host is still computing it.

RepoRef.description:
A repository on a code host, from its remote URL. `owner` is the whole
namespace — `acme`, or GitLab's `acme/platform` — and `slug()` the path
the host's API addresses the repository by.

ReviewSummary.description: A review submitted on a pull request, read back from the code host.

ReviewThread.description:
A resolvable inline conversation on a pull request. `id` is the code host's
opaque thread id, the handle [`CodeHost::resolve_review_thread`] acts on.

ReviewThreadComment.description: One comment inside a review thread, read from the code host.

PrThreadReply.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/pr/threads/{thread_id}/reply`: the person's
words on the thread, and whether the thread is resolved in the same act.

path.description: Project-relative path of the file the hunk is in.

hunk.description:
The hunk text as displayed; hashed into the note's identity and
carried as the chip an agent sees.

oneOf.description: Worktree against the index.
Index against HEAD.
HEAD against a base ref.

DiffScope.description:
Which diff a note or a hunk belongs to. Three different patches for one
path, so the side is always part of the reference.

diff_identity.description: Hash of the hunk text the note was written against.

hunk.description:
The hunk text itself, so the note can be handed on as a
`ContextRef::DiffHunk` chip and read by an agent without re-deriving a
diff that may no longer exist. Bounded by the writer; empty when the
note was written without one.

sent_at.description: Set when handed to an agent; cleared on edit.

resolved_at.description:
Set when the agent (or the person) marked the note as dealt with.
A resolved note stays on disk — it is the record that a remark was
acted on — and is hidden from the default listings.

RelPath.description: A path relative to a scope's root: no leading slash, no '..' component, forward slashes

LineRange.description: An inclusive 1-based line range. One line is a 1-length range.

oneOf.description: An `approval` step, an adoption or an amendment of a workflow.
A question raised from inside a run.
An outward action that cannot be taken back.

Gate.description:
Any gate a person may be asked to decide. The union the journal, the inbox
and the governance policy are keyed on.

oneOf.description: Approve or decline. The gates.

multi.description: Whether more than one option may be chosen.

oneOf.description:
The human tells you something. `options` may be empty — a free-text
question is still the right shape when the answer is not enumerable.

AskKind.description:
What kind of human input a question expects.

The option list lives *inside* the `Answer` variant rather than beside the
enum. A sibling `options` field would let `expects: Decision` carry a
populated option list — a state with no meaning that every reader would
have to decide how to ignore.

Attachment.description:
The whole of the Goal ⇄ Project relationship: one row per attachment.
Symmetric, and neither side owns the other. Attaching and detaching move
no bytes (invariant I14).

ChannelId.description: A channel id: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', '.', ':'

oneOf.description: A standing conversation the workspace can see.

A conversation with a restricted audience. A different set of
participants is a different channel.

Audience.description:
Who may read. `Workspace` uses the shared workspace key; `Restricted` is
wrapped pairwise to exactly those principals and never touches it.

oneOf.description:
Every enabled agent, every enabled team, every person. Stores no
list. Only `general` may hold this.

humans.description: The people the channel is for — what puts a guest in the room.

oneOf.description: Exactly these, intersected with enablement and membership when read.

RosterPolicy.description:
Who belongs. Evaluated at read time against enablement and membership —
never stored as a materialised list.

ChannelOrigin.description:
Where a channel came from. A separate type from [`crate::Origin`] because
exactly one channel is the platform's own.

oneOf.description: A person of the workspace, by pubkey.

Member.description: One member of a channel, as derived.

thinking.description:
An agent's reasoning before its words, when its harness said it
— kept beside the reply for a person who wants to read it; never
on a person's own post.

said.description:
The platform's own sentence, when the post is one — the Workflow
Agent's standing note — as data: the reader renders it in their
language, `text` being its English ([17](../../../docs/architecture/17-internationalisation.md)).
Never on a person's or an agent's own words.

oneOf.description:
The record that a membership change happened. Membership itself is derived
and stored nowhere; this is the history, which cannot be recomputed because
enablement is a boolean with no past.

MessageBody.description: The content of a kind-3407 event.

oneOf.description:
An element of a rendered page the person pointed at, and the change
they want for it (ide/03 §Annotate, ide/18). `page` is where the
element lives — a file of the project, or a URL the IDE's browser
showed; `excerpt` is the element as it was — the head of its HTML,
captured at send — and is the identity; `selector` is a locator hint
the page may have outgrown.

A device's screen the person captured and marked (ide/19): the
simulator, emulator or phone by id and name, the PNG as an attachment
the node holds, the rectangle they drew in device pixels — none for
the whole screen — and the change they want.

ContextRef.description:
A piece of context a person attached to a message. Every variant renders
as a chip; the bytes that matter are captured at send so a peer with the
same project can act on it.

CommitId.description: A git commit id, 40 or 64 lowercase hex chars

PageRef.description:
Where an annotated element lives (ide/18): a file of the project, when
the page is one the IDE renders or serves from the checkout, or a URL —
a page a dev server or the web put in the IDE's browser, whose source is
not a file the agent can name.

Mark.description: A rectangle on a captured screen, in device pixels from the top left.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex. The blob's address, and the proof of what it contains.

name.description:
What the maker called the file. Display and the named copy only —
never a path anything joins to a directory unsanitised.

title.description:
What it is called where it renders. The same title on a later post is
a new version of the same thing.

ArtifactRef.description:
One artifact on a message: an attachment's descriptor, a title, a kind,
and where it came from.

oneOf.description: A web page, rendered live in a sandbox.
A spreadsheet: csv, tsv, xlsx.
A word-processor document: docx.
A deck: pptx.
A Mermaid diagram source.
Source code, shown read-only with its language.
Structured data: json, yaml, toml, xml.
Bytes with a name and nothing to draw: the card alone.

ArtifactKind.description:
What an artifact is, and therefore how it is shown. Closed: the desktop
keeps one renderer per word and a test holds its list equal to this one.

ArtifactSource.description:
Where an artifact was written, when it was written inside a root the
desktop can open: the checkout a session worked in, or a goal's scratch.

oneOf.description:
A checkout: the project's own root (its primary workstream) or a
worktree or copy under it. There is no separate project
scope — a project's root *is* a workstream.

One unit of work, wherever it actually ran — its workstream checkout when
it has one, its home's scratch when it does not. The others name
a directory directly; this one names a *thing* and asks the workspace
where that thing's work happens.

A run of the workspace's own folder — the home a goal is for a goal's
run; its scratch is where a step with no project leaves what it made.

FileScope.description:
Which rooted thing a relative path is read under. The four roots the
desktop may name; every file route resolves one of them and checks
containment by canonicalisation.

oneOf.description:
The member's enablement flipped — the one change that produces a
membership event. A roster edited, a member made or removed produce
none: the roster is a directory and a membership is derived, so a
channel's list changes without a line in its timeline.

NamedFileBody.description: `POST /attachments/{sha256}/file`: the name the copy is made under.

photo.description:
The agent's picture — an attachment this machine holds, scaled by the
desktop, served by `GET /attachments/{sha256}?as=image` (ide/14
§Photos). Display only.

harness.description: Harness id this agent runs on.

models.description:
Ordered model candidates plus a strategy. Empty means "whatever the
harness runs by default".

skills.description:
Skill library ids, resolved at launch. A reference that no longer
resolves costs that skill and nothing else.

mcps.description: MCP registry ids, resolved at launch. Local; never synced.

decision_making.description:
Whether the Decision-Making Agent stands in at the decision points
this agent reaches — the pick of a pool it is in, the triage that may
wake it, its own `decide` tool — when the workspace has not switched it
on for all.

pubkey.description: The agent's own pubkey; the secret lives in the keystore.

origin.description:
Where this definition came from. No serde default: provenance that can
be omitted is provenance that can be laundered.

McpId.description: A mcp server id: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', '.', ':'

oneOf.description: Acts only on input from its attested owner (fail-closed default).
Acts on input from any workspace member.

RespondPolicy.description: Who an agent will act for.

oneOf.description: Created in this workspace.
Installed from the bundled catalog, under this slug.

The platform's own agent, one of the two that hold a record: always
present, never removable, and only its harness, its model plan and its
decision-making switch are editable.

AgentOrigin.description:
Where an agent came from.

A separate type from [`Origin`] because it has a third case the others
cannot hold: exactly one agent is the platform's own, and only an agent can
be. Folding both into one enum would mean a `Core` skill and a `Core` team
were representable and then validated away, and a type that permits an
invalid state and then rejects it is a worse type than one that does not.

photo.description: The team's picture — an attachment this machine holds (ide/14 §Photos). Display only.

members.description: Agents and humans. Never a team.

origin.description: Provenance, not a lock: an installed team is yours to edit.

home.description:
Where the item is filed — its run's home: the goal the run is for, or
a run of the workspace itself.

run.description:
The run and the step this item was created for. An item outside a run
is refused at preflight: nothing schedules work a workflow did not ask
for.

instructions.description: What to do, self-contained (a fresh session must be able to act on it).

project.description:
The project this item works in. `None` means the work names no project
and the item runs in its home's own `scratch/` directory. There is
deliberately no `cwd`: a spec that could name a directory could name
the workspace root.

harness_candidates.description:
The harnesses the item runs on, in order; the engine walks this chain
on `Unavailable`. What its step named — the author's word — and, for
a step that named none, empty until the item is taken: it then runs
on the harness of the agent that took it, else on
[`DEFAULT_HARNESS`], and says so here.

effort.description:
The step's effort pin — a level, or `auto` — the first link of the
chain. Absent means the model's own, the agent's plan, the setting.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema the structured result must satisfy (via `yield_result`).

assignees.description:
Who this item is *for*: the request. Joins the assignment union at the
nearest position and, when non-empty, wins alone.

agent.description:
The agent that actually ran this item — **written by the engine when it
picks, never accepted from a caller.**

spawn_allowlist.description: Agent ids this item may spawn as sub-work ("*" = any, empty = none).

result_attempts.description:
Results submitted that did not fit the contract; the last miss blocks
the item (`max_result_attempts`).

interruptions.description: Sessions on this item a restart cut short; the next session is told.

WorkItemSpec.description:
`deny_unknown_fields`: an item written by the plan-shaped code carried
`plan` and `criteria`, and this build refuses it rather than half-reading it.

oneOf.description: Claimed by a principal via a signed `kind:3402`; first valid claim wins.
Waiting on a gate, a human or a dependency.
Result submitted, awaiting verification.
Rejected with the verification evidence; re-runs as steering input.

project.description: Required — a workstream is always of a project, and lives under it.

name.description:
A label the person chose. `None` means "call me by my branch" (see
[`Self::label`]).

note.description: Free text the person keeps beside the workstream — what it is for.

kind.description: What stands behind the checkout, and therefore where it is.

goal.description:
The goal it was created *for*. History, not a live association: it
survives detaching the project from that goal. `None` for a branch
made in the IDE and for the primary.

board.description:
Its place on the Board — a column, a rank, a due date — nothing until
a person sets something (`board.rs`). A view over the workstream,
never its lifecycle: the column is not the state.

oneOf.description:
The repository's own root checkout. Exactly one per project, born with
it; its id is the project's ([`WorkstreamId::primary_of`]). It cannot
be closed or deleted — removing the project is the substitute.

A git worktree standing on `branch`, opened from a
[`WorkstreamSource`]; `base` is the branch the work returns to — what
the lifecycle diffs against and a pull request targets — and never a
fiction: a checkout of an existing branch records the base it was
given, not one it was cut from. The worktree *is* the isolation, it
persists, and the artifact is a commit.
A non-git project falls back to the isolation floor: a copy.

WorkstreamKind.description:
What stands behind a workstream's checkout. The path is not here on
purpose: the store derives it from the kind, so a record cannot name a
directory outside its project.

oneOf.description: A commit was attempted and refused; the tree is exactly as left.

Merged, and still naming the pull request it went in through — a
merged branch's PR is the record of how the work landed, and a surface
that forgets it the moment it succeeds cannot show what happened.

column.description: The column the person chose; `None` follows the lifecycle.

rank.description: The order within the column, meaningful only beside other ranks.

WorkstreamBoard.description: A workstream's place on the Board — nothing until a person sets something.

BoardColumn.description: The five columns, in the order the Board shows them.

DueDate.description:
A calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD` — a due date is a day, not an instant, so it
carries no time zone and reads the same on every machine.

Schedule.description:
A cadence as written: `every` so many seconds, or a `cron` expression in
a time zone (`tz`, UTC when absent) — exactly one of the two, which
validation holds it to (`ProblemKind::BadTimer`). Flat on the start's
table: `on = { event = "schedule", cron = "0 9 * * 1", tz = "Europe/Paris" }`.

in.description:
The conversation it lands in — a channel id, a direct channel's, a
conversation's or a goal's thread (a template); absent, anywhere.

mentions.description: It mentions this agent, team or person.

contains.description: Its text contains this, case-insensitively (a template).

MessageFilter.description:
A message posted into a conversation: where, by whom, mentioning whom,
saying what. Heard where conversation dispatch hears a message — after the
hold a message from another node waits in — and never an announcement.

name.description: The signal's name (a template).

SignalFilter.description:
A named signal — raised by an `emit` step, a session's `emit_signal`, a
person through the CLI or the node, an A2A task — with exact fields on its
payload.

project.description: Absent while the designer has not chosen one: a problem, never `""`.

glob.description: Only files matching this (`*` and `?`), for `files` (a template).

ProjectFilter.description:
A change in one project — never a path on a disk, which would mean
nothing on another machine.

RunFilter.description: A run that ended — of one workflow, or of any.

fields.description: Exact matches on the event's own fields (templates).

PlatformFilter.description:
One of the engine's own bus events, by topic (`goal.closed`,
`step.changed`) and exact fields — the advanced door, for what the other
events do not name.

oneOf.description: Stop the step and take the flows labelled with the boundary's name.

Post into a conversation beside the live step, as a `notify` step
does: into `scope` (the run's own conversation when absent), as
`author` (the Workflow Agent when absent).
Raise a named signal beside the live step, as an `emit` step does.

BoundaryAct.description: What a boundary does when its event is heard.

TagEntity.description:
What kind of object a tag files.

A typed enum rather than a bare string: an entity name is written in the
store, in the index, in `?entity=` and in the desktop, and a typo in any of
them would silently return an empty filter instead of an error.

oneOf.description: The default: a wider filter is the one people expect from a tag list.

TagMatch.description: Whether a multi-tag filter means "carries any of these" or "carries all".

workflow.description:
The workflow the goal will run: a workflow id, or the catalog slug of
an installed template. Absent on an auto or guided goal means the
Workflow Agent designs one; on a manual goal, that the person will.

inputs.description:
Inputs for the run. **Present** starts the run at once (with
`workflow`); absent records the goal and waits for `POST
/goals/{id}/run`.

mode.description:
How the goal moves — `auto` (the Workflow Agent designs and the
platform adopts, starts and repairs alone), `guided` (it proposes,
you adopt) or `manual` (you design on the Workflow tab). Absent takes
the workspace's `goals.default_mode`.

assignees.description:
Optional assignees, in `Assignee`'s wire form (`agent:<id>` /
`human:<hex>` / `team:<id>`), to carry the goal from the start.

documents.description:
Files given as the goal's initial context: the descriptors `POST
/attachments` answered, materialised under the goal's `documents/`
before anything runs. A hash this node does not hold refuses the
capture.

decision_making.description:
Whether the Decision-Making Agent stands in at the decision points a
run of this workflow reaches, whatever the workspace's switch says.

NewWorkflowBody.description:
`POST /workflows`, the body of `POST /goals/{id}/amend`, and
`POST /workflows/validate`: a definition without its record fields. A key
the definition does not have is a 400, never dropped. Also what a catalog
row carries for a workflow template (`CatalogEntryDto::workflow`), so the
same shape is read back as it is written.

workflow.description: A workflow id, or the catalog slug of an installed template.

definition.description:
A whole definition instead: recorded as **this goal's design**
(`WorkflowOrigin::Goal`), kept as a draft with its problems, and
pointed at. Exclusive with `workflow`.

revision.description:
With `definition`, the revision of the goal's design the caller
edited. Required once the goal has a design; a design that moved
since is a 409.

SetWorkflowBody.description:
`PUT /goals/{id}/workflow` — the workflow the next run uses. `null`
clears it.

PutWorkflowBody.description:
`PUT /workflows/{wfid}` — the edited definition and the revision it was
edited from. The stored copy must still be at `revision`; otherwise 409,
and nothing is written. The definition's fields are spelled here rather
than flattened in, because a flattened struct cannot refuse a key it does
not know — and a save must refuse one exactly as a create does.

error.description: The sentence, in the request's language (`Accept-Language`; English when none).

text.description:
The sentence as data — the catalog message and its arguments — for a
client that renders in its own language or switches on the id.

detail.description:
The typed facts behind a `code`, when it has any: a conflict's
`paths` and `in_progress`, a refused fast-forward's `ahead`/`behind`.

ErrorBody.description:
Every error body: the message; for a definition that cannot start, its
problems by step and kind (omitted when there are none); and, for the
refusals a client renders differently from one another, a `code` naming
which one it is (omitted otherwise). A status alone cannot tell them
apart — every refusal below is a 409 — and a client that guessed from the
status told people their project publishes manually when their branch had
simply never been pushed.

oneOf.description: The project's publishing policy is `manual`: nothing publishes from here.

The project is gated and the workstream belongs to no goal, so there
is nobody to ask.
The Publish gate was declined; nothing left the machine.

The branch has no commits beyond its base; there is nothing to push or
open a pull request for.
A commit was asked of a clean tree.

The workstream's state does not admit the transition (`cannot … a
workstream that is …`), the primary was asked to close or finish, or
the workstream is already closed.

A workstream was asked for from a pull request that is not open;
`detail.number` and `detail.state` say which and what it is.

A merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or pull stopped on conflicting
content; `detail.paths` names the files and `detail.in_progress` the
operation to resolve or abort.

A fast-forward-only pull met local commits; `detail.ahead` and
`detail.behind` say how far apart the branch and its upstream are.

An operation is already half-done in this checkout (`detail.in_progress`);
resolve or abort it before starting another.

Another git process — an editor, an agent's own `git` in a terminal —
holds the repository's lock; nothing was written. Try again once it
has finished. (The platform's own writers queue per checkout and never
meet each other here.)

A workstream script stood in the way (ide/07 §Workstream scripts): the
pre-create script refused the checkout, or the clean script kept it —
non-zero, timed out, or not approved on this machine. `detail.phase`
names which and `detail.output` is the tail of what it printed.

An approval or a change request on a pull request the connected account
itself opened; the code host takes only a comment from its author.
`detail.author` names the account.

A stash was asked of a tree with nothing it would save — clean, only
untracked files without *include untracked*, paths with no change, or
no commit yet. Nothing was written, no recovery ref included.

`stash@{index}` no longer holds the commit the caller saw there: the
list moved (a push or a drop here or in another worktree). `detail`
carries `index`, `commit` and `now` — what sits there today. Reload.

ErrorCode.description:
The refusals a client tells apart. Each names one producer that exists;
a message is still the words, the code is what a client switches on.

start.description:
The start step the run begins at — an event start, for a test run.
Absent, a person's run: at the manual entry.

event.description:
A test run's sample payload: the event its start's mapping reads, as
if it had happened.

StartRunBody.description:
`POST /goals/{id}/run` — make a run with these inputs: started at once,
or queued behind the goal's live run — and `POST /workflows/{wfid}/runs`,
a run of the workspace, started at once beside any other.

ReleaseStepBody.description:
`POST /runs/{rid}/steps/{step}/release` — let a held `wait` step go; a
payload, when given, is the step's output.

started_at.description: Unix seconds when the node started serving.

socket.description: The unix socket bound — the fallback path when the data dir is long.

listen.description: The loopback address, as a URL, when the node listens on TCP too.

paused.description: Nothing new starts while paused; running sessions finish.

live_sessions.description: Sessions going right now — workers, turns, terminals.

NodeInfo.description:
`GET /node`: what this node is — the process, where it listens, where it
keeps the workspace, whether the engine is paused and how many sessions
are live. The footer's node overlay reads it on open.

StopBody.description:
`POST /goals/{id}/stop` and `POST /runs/{rid}/stop` — stop the goal or
the run, with the person's word on why.

superseded_by.description: The goal that replaces this one, when there is one.

CloseBody.description:
`POST /goals/{id}/close`: its person's word on why, or the goal that
takes its place.

GovernanceBody.description:
`PUT /governance`: who may decide each gate. A gate left out keeps the
policy it has.

oneOf.description: Only the owner.
The owner and every admin.
The owner, every admin and every member — never a guest.

Exactly these entries: pubkey hex strings and/or `team:<id>` refs (a
team ref expands to the team's human members at check time). A listed
person still has to be a member who may decide gates.

purpose.description: What the team is for. `null` removes it.

members.description: The whole roster, replaced: `{"agent": id}` or `{"human": pubkey}`.

apply.description:
`false` previews; `true` applies to `files`, each with the hash its
preview carried.

IdeReplaceFile.description: One file a replace is applied to, as its preview read it.

OpenInteractiveBody.description:
`POST /sessions/terminal`: a harness a person is opening in a desktop
terminal — where (a file scope and its id) and which one.

ExitBody.description:
`POST /sessions/{id}/exit`: the process behind the session ended — with
this status, or by this signal, or (both absent) without saying.

remote.description: The remote to fetch; `origin` when omitted.
The remote to fetch first; `origin` when omitted.

PullModeBody.description: How a pull moves the branch once the fetch has landed.

StopOutcome.description:
What a stop did: the live run it cancelled and the queued runs it
withdrew — `POST /goals/{id}/stop`'s answer.

AmendBody.description:
`POST /goals/{id}/amend` — replace the steps of the current run that have
not started.

answer.description:
What the human said, for question gates. Carries the options they
picked, what they typed, and whether they said "I'm not sure" — a
third outcome that resolves the question without declining it.

oneOf.description:
Copy an existing folder into `goals/<owner>/projects/<slug>`, as a

`path` is validated exactly as `adopt` validates it — absolute,
canonicalized, an existing directory, and outside the Bisa
workspace. `.git` is copied, so an imported repository keeps its
history and its `vcs` is detected from the copy. Symlinks are skipped
rather than followed: a link pointing out of the source would turn an
import into a copy of whatever it targets. The copy is refused above a
size and entry bound, and refused outright if the destination folder
already exists.

whatever the source.

NewProjectBody.description:
`POST /goals/{id}/projects` — **provenance is explicit**.

There are exactly five ways a project comes into existence, and the caller
says which one it is rather than the node guessing from which fields are
present. A **managed** root — `new`, `clone`, `import` — is a folder this
node makes, so `new` initialises it as a repository and carries no flag for
it; `adopt` never writes anything into the folder it points at, which is
the half of the rule that stayed absolute.

`import` and `adopt` are the two answers to the same folder. `import`
copies the tree in and the files become the goal's; `adopt` points at it
where it lies and Bisa writes nothing into it, ever. Neither one
modifies the folder it was given — an import reads the source and writes
only inside the workspace.

PatchProjectBody.description:
`PATCH /projects/{pid}`. Omitted fields keep their current value.

The slug is not patchable: it is a directory name, and moving a folder
(possibly with live worktrees in it) is not something a record edit should
imply.

`group` and `photo` are **tri-state**: absent keeps the value, `null`
clears it, a value sets it — see [`clearable`].

ProjectAttachBody.description:
`POST`/`DELETE /projects/{pid}/attach` — the goal the project becomes
visible in (or stops being visible in).

goal.description:
Whose folder holds the checkout. Defaults to the project's owner; any
other goal must be able to *see* the project (own ∪ linked ∪
ancestors').

label.description: Human-readable half of the branch name (`work/<label>-<tail>`).

agent.description: Agent this workstream belongs to, for attribution in the journal.

source.description:
Where the checkout starts (ide/07 §Where a workstream starts): a new
branch (typed or derived, at a ref or the base), an existing local
branch, a remote's branch (fetched and tracked), a tag (a new branch
at it, the tag made first when `create_at` says where), or an open
pull request (its head tracked, its base as the base, the record born
linked). Absent: a derived new branch at the base.

base.description:
The branch the work goes back to; the project's default branch when
absent. A pull request source brings its own and ignores this.

oneOf.description:
A new branch: `name` as a person typed it (made safe, never refused)
or, absent, one derived from the label; `start` is the ref HEAD begins
at — the base when absent.
A branch that already exists in the repository, checked out as it is.

A branch on a remote: fetched, then a local branch of the same name
tracking it.

A tag: a new branch at it, `branch` when a person named one, else
`from/<tag>`. With `create_at`, the tag is made first, at that ref.

An open pull request on the code host behind `origin`: its head branch
fetched and tracked, its base as the base, the record born linked
([`WorkstreamTransition::PrAdopted`]).

WorkstreamSource.description:
Where a workstream **starts** — what branch its checkout stands on and
where that branch's HEAD begins (ide/07 §Where a workstream starts). This
is a different fact from the base: the base is where the work *goes back
to*; the source is where it *comes from*. A workstream is always a branch
and a checkout, one-to-one, so a tag or a commit opens a new branch at
that point rather than a detached HEAD.

On the wire the variant is the `source` word, so a request reads
`{"source":"local_branch","name":"topic"}`; the CLI spells the same thing
as a spec — `branch:topic`, `remote:origin/topic`, `tag:v1`,
`new-tag:v1@main`, `pr:12`, or a bare name for a new branch
([`FromStr`]).

name.description: A label; `null` goes back to calling it by its branch.

due.description: The Board's due date, `YYYY-MM-DD`; `null` clears it. A day, not an instant.

PatchWorkstreamBody.description:
`PATCH /workstreams/{wid}` — what a person may change about a workstream.
`name` and `note` are tri-state like a project's `group`.

index.description: Where among the column's cards, from the top; past the end is last.

PlaceWorkstreamBody.description:
`PUT /workstreams/{wid}/board/place` — put a card at an index in a Board
column. The engine turns the index into a rank; the reply is every record
that changed (one, or the whole column when it was renumbered).

draft.description: Only when the code host has draft pull requests.

StageBody.description:
`POST /workstreams/{wid}/git/stage` and `/workstreams/{wid}/git/unstage` — the
paths a person ticked, exactly as `GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/files` reported
them (relative to the repository root).

paths.description:
Staged first, then committed. **Empty means "commit what is already
staged"**, never "commit everything": a project's folder is the user's
own working tree and may hold edits that have nothing to do with this
commit.

inputs.description:
The inputs its start events read and do not map
(`WorkflowRow.listening_needs`), and any other it declares.

budget.description:
Each run's own ceiling; absent, the workspace default
(`budget.default.*`); `{}`, no ceiling whatever the default.

ListeningBody.description:
`PUT /workflows/{wfid}/listening` — turn a library workflow On: what its
event runs bind, and what each may spend.

inputs.description: What it listens with; absent, what it listened with before.

GoalListeningBody.description:
`PUT /goals/{id}/listening` — the goal listens, or listens again after a
failed run or a spent budget paused it. Its runs spend against the goal's
budget, so it names none.

name.description:
Dot-separated parts of lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`
(`report.ready`).

goal.description: The goal it is raised on; absent, the workspace.

EmitSignalBody.description:
`POST /signals` — raise a named signal: heard by the starts, waits and
boundary events that name it.

CatalogInstallBody.description:
`POST /catalog/install` — one entry, named by kind and slug.

The kind is a string rather than the enum so a typo is refused by the same
message `?kind=` gives, naming all five spellings, instead of by serde's
report of an unmatched variant.

mode.description: The goal's mode; the agent designs for `auto` and `guided` goals.

design_enabled.description: Whether this node designs at all (`EngineConfig::design_enabled`).

phase.description:
`design` while the Workflow Agent owes a proposal, `repair` after a
failed run, otherwise the goal's status.

design.description:
Where the Workflow Agent stands on that job — working, asking,
proposed, stalled, failed, off — from the goal's last guidance fact,
with `live` saying whether a wake is behind it right now. Absent when
no fact applies (a goal that was never guided, or one already running).

GuidanceInfo.description:
The Workflow Agent's standing over a goal — drives the goal page's
designing card and the "the Workflow Agent is asking…" strip.

since.description: Unix seconds the fact was recorded.

live.description: A wake is in flight on this node right now.

DesignStatus.description:
Where the Workflow Agent stands on a goal, for a screen: the last guidance
fact that still applies, and whether a wake is behind it right now.

oneOf.description: Propose the workflow for a goal that has none.
A run failed; propose the fix.

GuidancePhase.description:
Derives `JsonSchema` because the Pulse ships journal payloads to the desktop
verbatim: a payload the wire types describe is a payload the desktop's
`switch` must handle to compile.
Which of the Workflow Agent's two jobs a guidance fact is about.

oneOf.description: A wake is queued; it may sit here while the engine is paused.
A session launched and is working; `session` names it.
It asked the person something and waits for the answer.
A proposal landed and its gate opened.

It stopped without proposing: timed out, ended its turn, or was
interrupted by a restart. `detail` says which.

It could not start — the agent could not be resolved or launched, or
refused the prompt. `detail` says why.
Designing is off on this node; nobody will design.

GuidanceStatus.description:
Where the Workflow Agent stands on a guided goal. Every transition is one
journal fact and one bus event, written by a single funnel in the engine,
so a screen — and a restarted node — can tell *working* from *dead*.

home.description:
Where the decision is filed and decided through: the goal
(`POST /goals/{id}/decide`), or a run of the workspace
(`POST /runs/{rid}/decide`).

gate_id.description:
The live gate id. Absent when the pending decision was reconstructed
from the run (a waiting `human` or `approval` step) or the journal (an
adoption) — decide those through the home.

run.description: The run step this decision completes, when it completes one.

expects.description:
What input this gate expects — and, for an answer, the options the
asker offered. The escape hatches ("I'm not sure", free text) are the
platform's, not the asker's: they are valid on every answer gate
whether or not this list is empty.

durable.description:
True when this was reconstructed from durable state rather than a live
gate.

subject.description:
What is being decided — `approval:<run>/<step>`, `adopt:<workflow>@…`,
a branch and remote. Without it a row can only say "approval" and
never *what* is being approved, which is the half a person needs.

work_item.description:
Which work item is blocked. Five items run in parallel under one
goal; "a session is waiting on you" does not say which.

opened_at.description:
When the gate opened, or the step started waiting. Absent when neither
is known — an invented clock is worse than none, because a gate waiting
nine days would render as new and hide exactly the staleness worth
seeing.

proposal.description:
For an adoption: the proposed workflow itself — description, every
step with a one-line summary, edges, inputs — so the card that asks
*adopt?* shows what is being adopted, not a name and a count.

listening_needs.description:
What listening asks, when the design begins on events: the inputs its
event starts read and do not map, with no default to fill them — what
the card binds before adopting, in place of a run's inputs.

event_only.description: Only events begin it: adopting it makes the goal listen, never run.

ProposalView.description: A proposed workflow as the ask card renders it.

event.description:
A `start` step's event word (`StartOn::as_str`); `null` for any
other kind.

summary.description:
One line a person can judge the step by (`Step::summary`), as data — the
reader renders it in their language.

join.description: How the step's incoming flows are counted: `all`, `any` or `one`.

on_fail.description: What happens on failure when it is not "the run fails": `skip`, or `then <step>`.

ProposalStep.description: One step of a proposal, summarised for a reader.

problems.description: Why this definition cannot start as written. Empty when it can.

workspace_problems.description:
Why it cannot run in the workspace, beyond `problems`: a step that
reads `{goal.…}` has no goal to read there (`needs_goal`) — it runs
on a goal only. Empty when *Run…* can start it.

runs.description:
Its runs of the workspace, counted — what a card says and its verbs
are drawn from without a fetch per workflow.

used_by.description: The goals and workflows pointing at it — what a delete refuses over.

listening.description:
Its standing while it is On — the inputs its event runs bind, the
per-run budget, since when, why it paused; `null` while it is Off.

starts.description: One per `start` step, the manual one included: which event, in words.

event_only.description:
Only events begin it: it names starts and none is by hand — *Run…*
is a test run.

listening_needs.description:
What turning it On asks: the inputs its event starts read and do not
map, with no default to fill them.

WorkflowRow.description: A row of `GET /workflows`, and the flat body of `GET /workflows/{wfid}`.

WorkflowRuns.description:
A workflow's runs of the workspace on its row: how many are going, how
many it has had, and the newest.

goal.description: The goal whose run it is; absent for a run of the workspace.

number.description:
Its place among the runs of its goal — or of its workflow in the
workspace — oldest first, 1 the first: *run #3*.

workflow_name.description: The workflow's name as the run froze it.

started_by.description:
Who started it: a person, an event one of its start events heard, or a
test run — read from the run's event.

queued_at.description: When the run was made; the queue's order.

started_at.description: Absent while the run is queued.

cause.description: Why a cancelled run was cancelled.

position.description: A queued run's place in its goal's queue, 1 next.

RunSummary.description:
One run — a goal's or the workspace's — in a list: enough to draw a row
without the frozen workflow it carries.

oneOf.description: By hand: no event began it.
An occurrence one of its start events heard.

A test run: begun at a start as if its event had happened. `event`
is that start's event word (`StartOn::as_str`).

StartedBy.description:
Who started a run, as a list row says it: a person's *Run…*, an event one
of the workflow's start events heard — its kind, and a detail when there
is one (who sent the message, which signal, which run) — or a test run.

EventKind.description:
The kind of event that began a run: the start events' words, a person's
start and a test run apart.

StartSummary.description:
One way a workflow begins, as its row says it: the start step, its
event's word (`StartOn::as_str`) and the step's summary.

statement.description: A card needs something to say for an untitled goal.

run_unreadable.description:
The goal names a run this node cannot read — the file is gone, or
another shape of the code wrote it. `status`, `strip` and `holder`
are then drawn as for a goal with no run; this says why.

strip.description:
The run drawn as a strip: every step in definition order with its
state. A draft with a chosen or proposed workflow ghosts the
definition with every step pending.

holder.description:
Who the goal waits on — the word the Goals screen, the CLI and the
inbox share (`Goal::holder`).

run_status.description:
The current run's status, when the goal has one — what a list draws
a card's run verbs from (stop, restart, a new run) without a fetch
per goal.

queued.description: How many runs wait behind the live one.

last_activity_at.description: The newest step movement, else the run's start, else the goal's birth.

archived.description: Put away — a mark on a closed goal, never a status; a list shows it only when asked.

listening.description:
The goal's standing while its workflow begins on events: armed, or
paused after a failed run or a spent budget; `null` for a goal whose
work begins by hand.

GoalRow.description:
One goal on the `GET /goals` list — and the same row `GET /teams/{id}`
and `GET /goals/{id}` carry, so every screen reads one shape.

reached.description: Steps that reached an end state, over the total. The reader divides.

failure.description:
Where a failed run failed: the newest step in `failed`, with its
error — so a row and a banner say why without opening the run.

RunStrip.description:
A run flattened for a list row: the steps in definition order, the live
ones, and how far it got.

RunFailure.description: The step a run failed at, by id and name, and what it recorded.

next_due.description: When a timed or polled start next comes due, unix seconds.

last_fired_at.description: When it last heard its event, unix seconds.

backlog.description: Occurrences waiting in the durable backlog.

live_runs.description: Runs it started that are still going.

local_hook.description: A hook start's local route, called under the control-plane token.

public_hook.description: A public hook start's route and whether its secret is minted.

failed.description: Why it could not be armed, when it could not.

ListenerView.description:
One listener — a start event armed for a host — as `GET /listeners` and
the listening routes list it: what it listens for, when it next comes
due, what waits behind it, and how it is called when it is a hook.

PublicHook.description:
A public hook start's route — a path, never a URL: the host is whatever
tunnel the operator put in front of the node — and whether the secret
that guards it is minted. Never the secret.

path.description: The route a caller outside posts to.

HookSecret.description: A public hook's secret, as it is shown: once.

listener.description:
The listener it was raised for; absent for a named signal kept for
the waits that replay it.

name.description: A named signal's name, or a platform topic.

note.description: Why it was skipped, failed, or is waiting or held, when it says.

SignalView.description:
One queued or settled occurrence, as `GET /signals` lists it: the fact
and where it stands — never its payload, which a run's event carries.

oneOf.description:
Kept behind a run of its listener that is still going, or over its
listener's rate.

Waiting on a person: an outside payload the content screen would not
pass. `POST /signals/{id}/release` lets it through.

It began its run — or, a named signal with no listener, it is kept
for the waits that replay it.

SignalState.description:
Where a signal stands in the queue, as `GET /signals` reports it. Mirrors
the store's `SignalState` one variant at a time so the wire contract is a
decision here rather than a leak of an internal enum.

secrets.description: Absent when the start minted none.

GoalArmed.description:
What `POST /goals/{id}/run` answers when the start armed the goal rather
than running it: no run — the goal listens — where the goal stands, and
the public hooks' secrets the start minted, shown this once.

holder.description:
Who the run waits on (`WorkflowRun::holder`) — the word the goal
row and the Runs tab share.

needs_actions.description:
What the run owes a person: its live gates, else the asks rebuilt
from the run and its home's journal — decided through `home`.

RunView.description:
`GET /runs/{rid}`: one run, whole — a goal's or the workspace's — with
its place among its siblings, who it waits on and what it owes a person.

key.description:
The thing's own id: a goal, channel, conversation, workstream,
project or workflow ULID. A row is a thing, never an event.

source.description:
The tab the row sits under (`?source=`): its kind's, except a
conversation, which sits under what it is about.

origin.description:
What a conversation row is about — its origin — so the row can say
so; absent on every other kind.

read.description:
Whether **you** have read this row: your local watermark is at or past
its latest activity. Deliberately not derived from `unread_count`,
which counts messages and so cannot tell a conversation you have read
from one that never had a message in it.

handled.description:
Whether the decision this row was asking for has been made. A
workspace fact, so it reads the same for everyone — unlike `read`.

mentioned.description:
You were named here, from the durable `p`-tag index. Computed on every
row rather than only inside the mentions filter: "someone addressed
me" is a property of a row, and a filter is one use of it.

notices.description:
What happened to this thing that concerns a person — the newest
first, from the activity index (`notices::notice_of`), bounded.

unread_notices.description: The notices after your read watermark.

decided.description:
The most recent decision on record, so a handled row can say what was
decided instead of merely going quiet.

status.description: A goal row's status, read from its current run.

join.description:
A people row's open ask: somebody claimed an invitation under
`collab.join = ask` and waits to be admitted or refused here.

waiting.description: A `session` row's harness, waiting on you in its terminal.

oneOf.description: A direct channel.
A workstream: its scripts, its lifecycle on the code host.
A project: what was made for it and who commits in it.
A conversation: its thread named you or moved unread.

A workflow: what the Workflow Agent designed or proposed, its being
put away, and a listener of it that could not start its run. A
person's own save is no news to them. It has no conversation.

A person on another node (14-collaboration): asked to join, joined,
left, or said something the classifier held. Keyed by pubkey.

A harness a person opened in the IDE's terminal, waiting on them at
its own prompt (ide/06 §Reporting). Keyed by the session; a row only
while it waits.

InboxKind.description: The kinds of thing an Inbox row is.

InboxSource.description:
The tab an Inbox row sits under — what the row is *about*, not what kind
of record it is: a conversation about a goal is the goals'. The wire's
`?source=` takes these words, and every row carries its own, so nothing
mirrors the rule.

seq.description: The row's place in the feed — the keyset's tiebreak within a second.

concept.description: The concept the row belongs to — the filter it answers.

kind.description: The payload's tag, so a client can key a glyph or a filter without opening `event`.

source.description: What the row is about: the record a click opens.

title.description:
What that record is called — a goal's title, a channel's name, a
workstream's label. Its own field rather than interpolated into the
line, because a title buried in a sentence cannot be styled, cannot be
linked, and cannot be used to group consecutive rows under one heading.

author.description:
The signing principal, raw. Naming it is the client's job: the desktop
already resolves a pubkey to a member or agent name, and a name
resolved here would be a second, staler copy of that map.

NoticeDto.description:
One notice on a row: which kind of thing happened, and the fact itself
as the Pulse carries it — so the desktop words it with the same function
a Pulse row gets, and a door opens the same record.

oneOf.description: A step failed or blocked.
A work item spent its budget or its wall clock.
The Workflow Agent stalled or could not start.

A listener could not be armed, or a signal of it could not start its
run — on its host's row.
What a person approved at the Publish gate did not go out.
A workflow step made a project.
Somebody claimed an invite under `collab.join = ask` and waits.
A person on another node was admitted.
A person on another node left or was removed.
A person's message is held from agents by the classifier.

The Workflow Agent wrote a workflow — a proposal recorded, an
amendment applied alone. A person's own save is none.

The Workflow Agent proposed a revision for a goal. The Adopt gate is
the goal's ask; this is the workflow's story.

A workflow was put away — out of the library and the pickers. Taking
it back out is none.

NoticeKind.description: What kind of thing happened — the short, named list the Inbox reads.

oneOf.description: The workspace's own shape: a goal made, a note written.
A goal's story: its notes, questions, decisions, progress, results and runs.

Workflows designed, proposed, changed and turned on — and what their
start events heard.
Projects and their workstreams: made, edited, opened, committed, attached.
Messages in a channel, a direct message or a workstream thread.
Agents at work: claims, metrics, sessions scheduled and ended, replies, the guard.
This node: its settings, its git setup, paused and resumed.

ActivityConcept.description: The concepts a reader filters the feed by, in the order a surface lists them.

id.description: The record's id; empty for this node or the workspace itself.

PulseSource.description: The record a row is about.

oneOf.description: A conversation: its messages, whatever its origin.

ActivitySourceKind.description:
What a fact is about — the thing a row opens on. `Node` and `Workspace`
name no record; their id is the empty string.

PulseEvent.description:
What happened.

Untagged because every arm is already internally tagged on `type`, so the
union stays one flat discriminated shape on the wire. The journal arm
carries the payload **verbatim**: nothing here restates a variant's
fields, which is what makes it structurally impossible for a payload added
to the journal to reach the Pulse as anything less than itself. The engine
arm is the `EnginePayload` the frame carried, as recorded — the desktop's
hand-written mirror of that enum (`types.hand.ts`) is its type.

oneOf.description: Clarification or revision rationale (kind:3400).

The Workflow Agent's standing on a guided goal (kind:3400): which job
it is on and where it stands, so the design of a goal's workflow is
never a silence — a screen reads the last of these, and a restarted
node knows what was in flight.

The Tool & Commands Guard judged a tool call in this journal's goal or
run of the workspace (kind:3400):
what was asked, what was decided and by whom — a rule, the classifier
or a person. The subject is the **redacted** command or input; a
journal never carries a secret.

run.description: The run and the step it was asked for, when it was asked for one.

oneOf.description:
The Decision-Making Agent judged something in this journal's goal or
run of the workspace (kind:3400): which decision point asked, which
provider and model answered, the questions as they were asked
(redacted), the answers and what became of them.
Not a [`JournalPayload::Decision`]: a judgement never signs a gate.

subject.description:
What is being decided: `approval:<run>/<step>`, `adopt:<workflow>@<rev>`,
`amend:<run>@<rev>`, a result event id, an escalation id.

answer.description: What the human said, when the gate was a question.

oneOf.description: Signed gate decision (kind:3401).

A question raised for a human, awaiting a decision or an answer.
`expects` carries the options the asker offered, so the journal — not a
live gate — is what a restarted daemon re-renders the question from.

A question taken back before anyone answered — withdrawn by the
process that asked, or found by a restart with the asker dead. The
subject is the question's; a restarted daemon rebuilds no ask that a
later `Withdrawn` names.
Work-item claim (kind:3402).
Coarse progress (kind:3403) — the activity triple.

Structured result (kind:3404), already validated against the work
item's schema.

event.description:
Nested rather than flattened: a flattened tagged enum inside a
tagged enum is a schema the desktop's type generator cannot read
(it keeps the inner union and drops `type`, `run` and `step`), so
the fact travels as `event: { fact: "done", … }`.

oneOf.description:
One step of a run changed (kind:3411). The run snapshot is the state;
this is the rationale-bearing fact.

event.description: Nested for the same reason as [`Self::Step`]'s.

oneOf.description:
The run itself was queued, started, amended, finished or cancelled
(kind:3411).

A project was attached to (or detached from) this goal. The whole of
the Goal ⇄ Project relation is this fact and its author: it syncs with
the journal and the `goal_projects` cache is rebuilt from it.

A file a person gave the goal as context — a brief, a spec, a
screenshot — kept under the goal's `documents/` folder. The fact
carries the attachment descriptor: the bytes are content-addressed
and reach a peer by hash on demand, and the folder is materialised
from the facts wherever the bytes are held (kind:3400).

The occurrence that started a run (kind:3410), on the run's home: the
signal's id, the listener it was raised for, what kind of event it
was, its name when it had one, and what it carried.
Per-turn cost accounting (kind:3406, encrypted at the envelope layer).

PulseMessage.description:
A message in a conversation — a post or a membership change. A snippet,
not the body: the row is a pointer into the conversation, not a copy of
it. It carries `type: "message"` as an explicit field, so the untagged
union stays one flat shape discriminated on `type` in the schema as well
as on the wire.

EngineActivity.description: An engine fact as recorded — the frame's payload verbatim; the desktop's hand-written `EnginePayload` is its type.

gate_kind.description:
The journal stores a gate's kind as its Rust name. Parsing that back
is not a round-trip anything guarantees, so an unrecognised label
yields `None` — a generic glyph beats a confidently wrong one.

Decided.description:
A decision that has already been made on a conversation.

Read is per-person; *handled* is not. Whether a contract was approved is a
fact about the workspace, so the row says what was decided to everyone who
can see it rather than clearing itself for the one person who clicked.

session.description: The session's id on the roster — the row's key too.

harness.description: The harness id, as the catalog names it.

on.description: What it waits on, as the roster says it.

words.description: The wait in words — *permission: Bash*, *a question: …*.

subagent.description:
The sub-agent whose wait it is, by name, when a sub-agent asks and
not the session itself — the card reads *↳ explore · permission:
Bash*. Absent for the session's own wait.

since.description: Unix seconds the wait began — the sub-agent's when it is its wait.

WaitingSession.description:
A harness a person opened in the IDE's terminal, waiting on them at its
own prompt (ide/06 §Reporting) — the `session` row's one fact. The row
is there while the wait is and gone when the prompt is answered or the
tab closes; its door is the workstream's terminal in the Project IDE,
where the wait is answered — nothing here decides it.

oneOf.description:
The harness asked before running a tool; `gate_id` once the engine has
opened the escalation gate a person answers in the Inbox.
A step's own gate — an approval or an escalation the run raised.

WaitingOn.description: Why a session is waiting on a person.

ConversationKind.description:
Which message stream a surface reads and writes — a goal's thread, a
channel, a direct channel or a conversation (13 — Conversations). The
desktop's `Conversation` component takes one; a workstream or a project
has none of its own.

seq.description: The row's place in the feed — the keyset's tiebreak within a second.

concept.description: The concept the row belongs to — the filter it answers.

kind.description: The payload's tag, so a client can key a glyph or a filter without opening `event`.

source.description: What the row is about: the record a click opens.

title.description:
What that record is called — a goal's title, a channel's name, a
workstream's label. Its own field rather than interpolated into the
line, because a title buried in a sentence cannot be styled, cannot be
linked, and cannot be used to group consecutive rows under one heading.

author.description:
The signing principal, raw. Naming it is the client's job: the desktop
already resolves a pubkey to a member or agent name, and a name
resolved here would be a second, staler copy of that map.

PulseRow.description:
One thing that happened, carried as facts rather than as a finished
sentence.

The prose used to be composed here and shipped as `text`, which threw the
event's type away before the client ever saw it. A stored row could then
only guess its glyph from where it pointed, so a criterion failure and a
note drew the same symbol; a verification could say it failed but not what
the evidence was; and `TurnMetrics` — which both the CLI and the live activity timeline
render — produced no row at all. Live rows meanwhile *were* rendered from
their payload, so one event looked one way as it arrived and another way
after a reload. Shipping the payload leaves exactly one renderer, on the
client, and removes that divergence rather than papering over it.

PulsePage.description:
One page of the activity feed: the rows, newest first, and where the next
page starts — `null` on the last one.

PulseCursor.description:
Where a page stopped: the last row's `(at, seq)`, sent back as
`?before=&before_seq=` for the page after.

SessionsResponse.description: `GET /sessions`: every session's presence, the engine's own shape.

DrawingPending.description: A request the desktop has not answered yet.

oneOf.description: An agent step's work item.
A guided wake: the Workflow Agent designing or repairing a goal's workflow.
One turn of a conversation, reached only through it.

A harness a person opened in a desktop terminal, reporting through its
own hooks; never driven by the engine, never recorded here.

SessionKind.description:
What a session is a run of: the durable answer to "what kind of session
was this?", written when the row is. One vocabulary for the store, the
engine's roster and the wire.

oneOf.description: Launched; nothing has arrived from the harness yet.
Between turns.
A turn is running and no tool is.

A tool is running — and how heavy a hand it has (the rail
draws a glyph per tier, so a person sees *reading* from *executing*
without reading the tool's name).
Stopped until a person acts.
Disposed but resumable.

SessionState.description:
What a session is doing, as a person reads it. The same nine words on the
rail, the Agents pane, the Agents screen, the pet and the activity.

since.description: Unix seconds the current state was entered.

started.description:
Unix seconds the sub-agent was announced or first seen — never reset,
unlike `since`. The anchor the desktop counts its elapsed time from.

SubagentPresence.description:
A sub-agent a harness spawned inside a session, folded from
`SubagentStarted`, the `Nested` events under it, and `SubagentEnded`.

SubagentId.description:
A harness's own id for a sub-agent it spawned — Claude Code's `Task`
tool-use id, say. Opaque; only equality matters.

oneOf.description: The step was cancelled or amended away while the item ran.

ExecutionOutcome.description:
How a work item's execution ended — typed, so a screen matches a tag and
never a sentence.

args_summary.description: Short rendering of the arguments, already truncated by the adapter.

input.description:
The tool's raw input as the harness carries it — what the guard
reads a command and its paths from, and what an `Allow` may hand
back rewritten. `Null` when the harness does not say.

oneOf.description: May this tool run? Answered `Allow` or `Deny`.
The agent asked the person something. Answered `Text`.

The harness needs a sign-in it cannot do itself. Answered `Allow` once
the person has done it, or `Deny`.

InputRequestKind.description: What kind of input a harness stopped for.

oneOf.description: Into the OS trash, where a person can get it back.
Gone.

Disposal.description: How a delete disposes of the bytes.

git.description:
The path is a git repository *on disk* — the disk is the authority,
not the record.

exists.description: The folder is there at all.

branch.description: Short branch name; absent when HEAD is detached or unborn.

head.description: HEAD's commit; absent in a repository with no commits yet.

ahead.description: Commits HEAD has that the upstream lacks (zero without an upstream).

behind.description: Commits the upstream has that HEAD lacks (zero without an upstream).

in_progress.description: A merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert git has left half-done here.

error.description: Why git could not be asked, when it could not be.

GitStatusInfo.description:
A working tree's git state — counts and pointers, never file contents.

Neutral (`git: false`, everything zero, `clean: true`) for a project with
no repository, which is a legitimate kind of project rather than an error.

kind.description:
added | modified | deleted | renamed | copied | type-changed | unmerged
| unknown

ChangedFile.description: One changed file in a workstream, against HEAD.

path.description:
Relative to the repository root — hand it straight back to
stage/unstage/diff.

old_path.description: Where a rename or copy came from.

index.description:
Index against HEAD: `.` unmodified, `?` untracked, else git's letter
(`M`, `A`, `D`, `R`, `C`, `T`, `U`).

worktree.description: Worktree against the index, same alphabet.

conflicted.description: An unmerged path. Neither staged nor unstaged: resolve it first.

conflict.description:
What kind of conflict, for an unmerged path: which side changed,
added or deleted it (git's words — `us` is the current branch, under
a rebase the branch rebased onto).

GitFileRow.description:
One row of `GET /workstreams/{wid}/git/files`: a path and the two letters git
uses for it.

The letters are kept apart rather than folded into one verdict because a
file can be staged *and* modified again since, and a person staging by hand
is entitled to see that. `staged`/`unstaged` are the derived answers most
of the UI actually wants.

total.description:
Summed across every kind counted. With `?entity=`, that is the one
kind asked for.

TagFacet.description:
A row of `GET /tags`: one tag, how many objects carry it, and which kinds
they are — enough to draw a filter chip and know what it narrows.

TagEntityCount.description: One entity kind's share of a tag — a row of [`TagFacet::entities`].

CatalogKind.description:
What kind of definition a catalog entry is: the five values `?kind=` and
`POST /catalog/install` accept.

slug.description: The slug, which is also the id the entry installs under.

requires.description:
What installing this pulls in with it — agent slugs for a team, a
channel or a workflow's steps, skill slugs for an agent, and
`workflow:<slug>` for the templates a workflow's `spawn` steps start. A
picker can say what a choice costs before it is made.

installed.description:
Whether an object with this id already exists here. It says the id is
taken, not that this entry took it: an id held by something you created
reads as installed and the install refuses it rather than overwriting.

workflow.description:
A workflow template's whole definition — inputs, steps, flows — so a
gallery draws its graph before it is installed; absent for every other
kind. A `spawn` step whose target is not installed names a placeholder
id: the picture is drawn, the install resolves the reference.

CatalogEntry.description:
A row of `GET /catalog`: one installable definition, and whether its id is
already taken here.

workflows.description:
A workflow's id is a ULID, so the caller that wants to open what it
just installed needs the slug and the id both.

Installed.description:
What `POST /catalog/install` created, by kind.

Only creations. An entry already present is left exactly as it is and
appears nowhere here, so installing the same thing twice answers with every
list empty — that is idempotence reported honestly, not a failure.

oneOf.description: Where a goal's sessions run when the work names no project.
A note's truth file.
A work item's captured result: the patch a copy workstream left.
The signed event log.
An addressable snapshot.
A file a person gave the goal as context (`documents/`).

FileEntryKind.description:
What an entry *is*, not merely what it is called.

This is the point of the tree route. A goal's folder annotated this way
reads as the life of that goal — what it plans against, where its work
ran, what it produced — rather than as a directory dump. `dir` and `file`
are the honest fallback for everything inside somebody's own source tree.

path.description:
Relative to the scope's root and `/`-separated — always to the root,
never to whatever sub-path was listed, so a client hands it straight
back as `?path=`.

symlink.description:
Listed, never descended into. Omitting it would make the listing lie
about what is in the directory; following it would leave the root.

modified.description: Seconds since the epoch, when the filesystem will say.

ignored.description: Matched by the root's ignore rules: dimmed by the explorer, never hidden.

root.description:
The absolute root the listing is relative to. The same path
`/placement/{scope}/{id}` reports, so the two routes can be checked
against each other.

path.description: What was listed, relative to `root`. Empty means the root itself.

depth.description: How deep this listing actually went, after clamping.

truncated.description: The entry budget cut this listing: what is here is not all of it.

deeper.description:
There are entries below the depth asked for. A one-level listing of a
folder with subfolders says so; a client lists them when opened.

FileTree.description: `GET /tree/{scope}/{id}` — a bounded listing under one root.

path.description:
As asked for, relative to the root — not the absolute path, which would
put the workspace's location into every response.

size.description: The file's real length, which is larger than `text` when `truncated`.

binary.description:
No bytes are served for a binary file: there is nothing a caller could
do with a JSON string of a PNG except render mojibake. Detected from the
bytes, never from the extension.

Placement.description:
`GET /placement/{scope}/{id}` — where a scope's files live.

`exists: false` is an answer rather than an error. A project whose folder
has not been created and a project id nothing knows about are different
problems, and this is the route that keeps them apart.

since.description: Unix seconds the current state was entered.

effort.description:
The effort the session runs at: what it was launched with, after the
fit to its model. Absent when the harness takes none for the model,
and for a terminal session, which is the person's own.

agent.description:
The agent definition running, when one is — a chat persona, the
Workflow Agent, an assigned worker. `None` for a bare worker.

conversation.description:
The conversation this session is a turn of — the door every surface
reaches it through; never drawn as a row of the checkout it stands in.

run.description:
The run whose work item the session works on — how the roster names
a run of the workspace's worker, which no goal holds.

started.description:
Unix seconds the session was registered — never reset, unlike `since`.
The anchor the desktop measures total open time and a run's
completed-in duration from.

pid.description:
The harness process's OS pid while a turn runs — the root the desktop
traces a listening port to. Set on `ProcessStarted`, cleared
when the session ends or parks.

last_activity.description: Unix seconds of the last event, tokens included.

revision.description:
Climbs by one on every change a reader sees — each frame of a row
carries a higher number than the one before it, whatever order they
reach a reader in. A reader keeps the highest it has.

SessionRow.description: One live (or recently ended) harness session, as the roster shows it.
